semin-durr:77-77.t:
His saying: {استطعمآ أَهْلَهَا}: the jawāb (answer) of «إذا», i.e. they asked them for food. Regarding the repetition of «أهلَها» there are two views. The first: it is tawkīd (emphasis), of the type of putting the overt noun in place of the pronoun, as in the poet's saying:
318 - 4- لا أرى الموتَ يَسْبِقُ الموتَ شيءٌ ... نغَّصَ الموتُ ذا الغِنى والفقيرا
(I see nothing outstripping death; death has embittered the life of the rich and the poor alike.)
The second: it is for establishing (taʾsīs) a new meaning. That is because the people who were come to were not all the people, but only some of them, since it is not customarily possible for the two of them to come to all the people at one time. So when He mentioned the asking for food, He mentioned it in relation to all the people, as though the two of them went after the people one by one. Had it been said "استطعماهم", it would have been possible that the pronoun refers back to that part who were come to, to the exclusion of others; so He repeated "the people" for that reason.
His saying: {أَن يُضَيِّفُوهُمَا} is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of His saying «أبَوْا». The generality of readers read it with the doubled letter (tashdīd), from ضَيَّفَه يُضَيِّفه. Al-Ḥasan, Abū Rajāʾ and Abū Razīn read it without doubling, from أضافَه يُضيفه; the two are like مَيَّله and أماله.
His saying: {أَن يَنقَضَّ} is the object of the "wanting". «انقَضَّ» may have the pattern infaʿala, from the swooping (inqiḍāḍ) of the bird, or from al-qiḍḍa, which is small pebbles; the meaning then is: it wants to crumble like pebbles. From this comes "طعامٌ قَضَضٌ" when food has small pebbles in it. Or its pattern may be ifʿalla, like iḥmarra, from al-naqḍ: one says نَقَضَ البناءَ يَنْقُضُه when he demolishes the building. This is supported by what is in the copy (ḥarf) of ʿAbd Allāh and the reading of al-Aʿmash, «يريد ليُنْقَضَ», passive and with the lām, like the lām in His saying {يُرِيدُ الله لِيُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 26]. What Ubayy read is likewise, except that it is {يُرِيدُ أَن يُنقَضَ} without the lām of kay (purpose).
Al-Zuhrī read «أنْ يَنْقَاضَ» with an alif after the qāf. Al-Fārisī said: "It is from their saying قِضْتُه فانقاضَ", i.e. I demolished it and it was demolished. I say: on this view its pattern is yanfaʿil, the origin being انْقَيَض, and the yāʾ was replaced by an alif. When Abū al-Baqāʾ transmitted this reading he said: "like يَحْمارّ"; what this comparison requires is that its pattern be yafʿālla. Abū al-Baqāʾ also transmitted that it was read thus with the ḍād undoubled; he said: "It is from your saying انقاضَ البناءُ when the building collapsed."
ʿAlī, the Commander of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with him, and ʿIkrima among others read «يَنْقاص» with the undotted ṣād; it is from قاصَه يَقِيْصُه, i.e. he broke it. Ibn Khālawayh said: "The Arabs say انقاصَتِ السِّنُّ when the tooth splits lengthwise." And a verse of Dhū al-Rumma was recited:
318 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . . مُنْقاصٌ ومُنْكِثبُ
(… split apart and heaped up.)
It was also said: [it is said] when it cracks in any way. And a verse of Abū Dhuʾayb was recited:
3186 - فِراقٌ كقَيْصِ السِّنِّ، فالصَّبْرَ إنَّه ... لكلِّ أُناسٍ عَثْرَةٌ وجُبورُ
(A parting like the splitting of a tooth — so patience! For every people there is a stumble and a mending.)
Attributing wanting to the wall is majāz (figurative usage), and this is very widespread. Whoever denies majāz absolutely, or in the Quran specifically, interpreted it as meaning that life and will were created for the wall as for animals, or that the wanting issued from al-Khaḍir so that he and Moses would experience wonder. This is a great strain. Al-Zamakhsharī came down hard on whoever said this, in eloquent terms.
His saying: «لاتَّحّذْتَ»: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «لتَخِذْتَ» with fatḥa on the tāʾ and kasra on the khāʾ, from تَخِذَ يَتْخَذُ like تَعِبَ يتعَبُ. The rest read «لاتَّخَذْتَ» with the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl), doubling of the tāʾ and fatḥa on the khāʾ, from al-ittikhādh. [Translator's note: the lemma is printed «لاتَّحّذْتَ» with ḥāʾ; translated as written.] There is disagreement: are both from al-akhdh, the tāʾ being a substitute for the hamza, then the first tāʾ is dropped so that one says تَخِذَ, like تَقِيَ from اتَّقَى, as in:
318 - 7-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَقِ اللهَ فينا والكتابَ الذي تَتْلُوْ
(… fear Allah regarding us, and the Book that you recite.)
Or are both from تَخِذَ with the tāʾ original, their patterns being faʿila and iftaʿala? There are two views, whose verification has preceded in this place. [Translator's note: «في هذا الموضوع» as written; probably «في غير هذا الموضع» ("elsewhere") is meant.] The verb here, on both readings, is transitive to one object, because it means "earning".

semin-durr:78-78.t:
His saying: {فِرَاقُ بَيْنِي}: the generality of readers read it with iḍāfa (genitive construct), by extension of usage (ittisāʿ) in the ẓarf (adverb). It was also said: it [«بين»] means "connection" (al-waṣl). Similar to it is the poet's saying:
318 - 8-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وجِلْدَةُ بين العَيْنِ والأَنْفِ سالِمُ
(… and the skin between the eye and the nose is sound.)
Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «فِراقٌ» with tanwīn, according to the original. The repetition of the muḍāf ilayhi conjoined with wāw is what made it permissible to annex «بَيْنَ» to something that is not plural: do you not see that if you said only "المالُ بيني" it would not be a sentence until you say "بيننا" or "بيني وبين فلان"? Ibn Waththāb read «سَأُنْبِيْكَ» with a pure yāʾ in place of the hamza.

semin-durr:79-79.t:
His saying: {لِمَسَاكِينَ}: the generality of readers read it with the sīn undoubled, the plural of «مِسْكين». ʿAlī, the Commander of the Believers — may Allah honour his face — read it with the sīn doubled, the plural of «مَسَّاك». On this there are two views. The first: it is the one who holds the rudder (sukkān) of the ship; this has some appropriateness. The second: it is the one who tans al-musūk, the plural of «مَسْك» with fatḥa on the mīm, which is hides. This is far-fetched, because of His saying {يَعْمَلُونَ فِي البحر}. I do not think it is anything but a distortion attributed to the Commander of the Believers. «يَعْملون» is a ṣifa (adjective) of «مساكين».
His saying: {وَرَآءَهُم مَّلِكٌ}: «وراء» here — it was said that place is meant, and it was said time. There is also disagreement about it: is it in its literal sense, or does it mean "in front of"? For this second view they recited:
318 - 9- اليس ورائي أَنْ أَدِبَّ على العَصا ... فَيَأْمَنَ أعدائي ويَسْأَمَني أَهْلي
(Is it not ahead of me that I creep along on a staff, so my enemies feel safe and my family grows weary of me?)
And the saying of Labīd:
319 - 0- أليس ورائي إنْ تراخَتْ مَنِيَّتي ... لُزومُ العَصا تُحْنَى عليها الأصابعُ
(Is it not ahead of me, if my death is delayed, to cling to a staff with fingers bent over it?)
And the saying of Sawwār ibn al-Muḍarrib al-Saʿdī:
319 - 1- أَيَرْجُو بنو مروانَ سَمْعي وطاعتي ... وقومي تميمٌ والفلاةُ ورائيا
(Do the Banū Marwān hope for my hearing and obedience, while my people are Tamīm and the open desert lies before me?)
Similar to it is the saying of the Exalted: {مِّن وَرَآئِهِ جَهَنَّمُ} [Ibrāhīm: 16], i.e. in front of him.
His saying: «غَصْباً»: there are several views on it. One: it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial); or it is accusative as a maṣdar clarifying the kind of taking; or it is accusative as a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), which is far-fetched in meaning. Al-Zamakhsharī claimed that there is fronting and postponement in the speech; he said: "If you say: His saying «فَأَرَدْتُ أَنْ أعيبَها» is caused by the fear of its being seized, so its due was to come after the cause; why then was it put before it? I say: it is intended to come after, and was only put first because of the concern for it, and because the fear of seizure is not the cause by itself, but together with its belonging to the poor; so it is like your saying: زيدٌ ظنِّي مقيمٌ."

semin-durr:80-80.t:
His saying: {فَكَانَ أَبَوَاهُ مُؤْمِنَيْنِ}: the dual is by taghlīb (giving predominance), meaning his father and his mother; the masculine was given predominance, and this is widespread. Similar to it are al-qamarān (the sun and the moon) and al-ʿUmarān. It has preceded in [Sūrat] Yūsuf that "the two parents" there means the father and the maternal aunt; this one is closer.
The generality of readers read «مُؤْمِنَيْنِ» with yāʾ. Abū Saʿīd al-Khudrī and al-Jaḥdarī read «مؤمنان» with alif. On this there are three views. The first: it is according to the dialect of Banū al-Ḥārith and others. [Translator's note: printed «بين الحارث»; read as «بني الحارث».] The second: in «كان» there is the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and «أبواه مؤمنان» is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and khabar (predicate) in the position of the accusative, as in the poet's saying:
319 - 2-إذا مِتُّ كان الناسُ صِنْفانِ شامِتٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(When I die, people will be of two kinds: one gloating …)
This too admits both views. The third: in «كان» there is the pronoun of the boy, i.e. "so the boy was …", and the clause after it is the khabar. This is the best of the views.

semin-durr:81-81.t:
His saying: {أَن يُبْدِلَهُمَا}: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr read it with fatḥa on the bāʾ and doubling of the dāl, from «بَدَّلَ», here, and in al-Taḥrīm {أَن يُبْدِلَهُ}, and in al-Qalam {أَنْ يُبْدِلَنا}. The rest read with sukūn on the bāʾ and undoubled dāl, from «أَبْدَلَ», in the three places. It was said: they are two dialects with one meaning. Thaʿlab said: al-ibdāl is removing one substance and bringing another in its place. And he recited:
319 - 3- عَزْلَ الأميرِ للأميرِ المُبْدَلِ ... 
(Like the emir's dismissal of the emir who is replaced …)
He said: Do you not see that he removed one body and put another in its place? And al-tabdīl is changing the form into another, while the substance itself remains. Al-Farrāʾ argued from the saying of the Exalted: {يُبَدِّلُ الله سَيِّئَاتِهِمْ حَسَنَاتٍ} [al-Furqān: 70]. He said: "What Thaʿlab said is good, except that they make أبدلتُ mean بدّلتُ." [Translator's note: as written, al-Farrāʾ (d. 207) is made to comment on Thaʿlab (d. 291), who was later; the attribution is translated as it stands.] I say: from this, people disagreed about the saying of the Exalted: {يَوْمَ تُبَدَّلُ الأرض} [Ibrāhīm: 48]: do the body and the attribute change, or the attribute without the body?
His saying: «رُحْماً»: Ibn ʿĀmir read «رُحُماً» with two ḍammas; the rest with a ḍamma and sukūn; both mean mercy. Ruʾba said:
319 - 2- يا مُنْزِلَ الرُّحْمِ على إدْريسا ... ومُنْزِلَ اللَّعْنِ على إِبْليسا
(O You who send down mercy upon Idrīs, and send down the curse upon Iblīs.)
It was also said: al-ruḥm means al-raḥim (kinship); this is fitting here because of kinship through birth. This is supported by the reading of Ibn ʿAbbās, «رَحِماً», with fatḥa on the rāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ. «زكاة ورُحْماً» are both accusative as tamyīz (specification).

semin-durr:82-82.t:
His saying: {رَحْمَةً}: on it there are three views. The clearest: it is a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose). The second: it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent, i.e. He willed that being merciful; and it is a permanent (lāzima) ḥāl. The third: it is accusative in the manner of a maṣdar (verbal noun), because the meaning of {فَأَرَادَ رَبُّكَ أَن يَبْلُغَآ} is the meaning of «فَرَحِمَهما».
His saying: «تَسْطِعْ»: it was said that its origin is استطاع, and the tāʾ of iftiʿāl was dropped. It was also said: what was dropped is the original ṭāʾ, then the tāʾ of iftiʿāl was changed into ṭāʾ after the sīn; this is a far-fetched strain. It was also said: the sīn is added as compensation for changing the wāw into alif, the origin being أطاع. There is another place for verifying the discussion of it.
One also says «استتاعَ» with two tāʾs, and «اسْتاعَ» with one tāʾ; so these are four dialects, which Ibn al-Sikkīt reported.

semin-durr:83-83.t: His saying: {مِّنْهُ ذِكْراً}: i.e. some of his reports and story.

semin-durr:84-84.t: His saying: {إِنَّا مَكَّنَّا لَهُ}: its object is omitted, i.e. his affair and what he wants.

semin-durr:85-85.t: His saying: {فَأَتْبَعَ}: Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «فَأَتْبَعَ» and «ثم أَتْبَعَ» in the three places with the connecting hamza and doubling of the tāʾ. [Translator's note: the words are printed with the cutting hamza, but the description (connecting hamza, doubled tāʾ) indicates «فاتَّبع» / «ثم اتَّبع».] The rest read with the cutting hamza (hamzat al-qaṭʿ) and sukūn on the tāʾ. It was said: they have one meaning, and both are transitive to one object. It was also said: «أتبع» with the cutting hamza is transitive to two objects, one of which is omitted, its implied form being: "so he made a means follow another means", or "so he made his affair follow a means". From this is {وَأَتْبَعْنَاهُم فِي هَذِهِ الدنيا لَعْنَةً} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 42], where He made it transitive to two; and of the omission of one of the two objects is the saying of the Exalted: {فَأَتْبَعُوهُم مُّشْرِقِينَ} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 60], i.e. they made their troops follow them. Abū ʿUbayd chose «اتَّبع» with the connecting hamza; he said: "because it is about travelling." He said: "You say تَبِعْتُ القومَ and اتَّبَعْتُهم. As for al-itbāʿ with the cutting hamza, its meaning is catching up, as in the saying of the Exalted: {فَأَتْبَعَهُ شِهَابٌ ثَاقِبٌ} [al-Ṣāffāt: 10]." Yūnus and Abū Zayd said: «أَتْبَعَ» with the cutting hamza expresses one who is earnest, hastening, urgent in pursuit; whereas with the connecting hamza it only implies following in the tracks, without these qualities.

semin-durr:86-86.t:
His saying: {حامِيَةٍ}: Ibn ʿĀmir, Abū Bakr and the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it with an alif and a pure yāʾ after the mīm. The rest read without alif and with a hamza after the mīm. [Translator's note: printed «ضريحة»; read as «صريحة» ("pure").] As for the first reading, it is the active participle of حَمِي يَحْمِي, and the meaning is: in a hot spring. Abū ʿUbayd chose it; he said: "because a group of the Companions read it," and he named them. As for the second, it is from al-ḥamʾa, which is mud.
Ibn ʿAbbās was with Muʿāwiya. Muʿāwiya read «حاميةٍ», and Ibn ʿAbbās said: «حَمِئَةٍ». Muʿāwiya asked Ibn ʿUmar: "How do you read?" He said: "Like the reading of the Commander of the Believers." So Muʿāwiya sent and asked Kaʿb, who said: "I find it [in scripture] setting in water and mud." So he agreed with Ibn ʿAbbās. A man who was present there recited the saying of Tubbaʿ:
319 - 5- فرأى مغيبَ الشمسِ عند مآبِها ... في عينِ ذي خُلُبٍ وثَأْطٍ حَرْمِدِ
(He saw the setting place of the sun at its return, in a spring of slime and black, foul mud.)
There is no contradiction between the two readings, because the spring combines both descriptions: heat and its being of mud.
His saying: {إِمَّآ أَن تُعَذِّبَ}: in {أَن تُعَذِّبَ} the nominative is permissible as a mubtadaʾ (subject) with the khabar (predicate) omitted, i.e. "either your punishing is to happen"; or the nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is your punishing". And the accusative, i.e. "either you do [the act of] punishing". [Translator's note: the source prints «أَنْ تُعَذَّبَ» (passive) in the implied form; the active «أن تُعَذِّبَ» seems intended.]

semin-durr:88-88.t:
His saying: {جَزَآءً الحسنى}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «جزاءً» accusative with tanwīn; the rest read it nominative, in iḍāfa (genitive construct). The accusative is as a maṣdar (verbal noun) confirming the content of the clause, so it is made accusative by an implied [verb]; or as confirming an implied governing word from its own root, i.e. "He rewards [them] a reward", the clause then being parenthetical between the mubtadaʾ (subject) and its khabar (predicate), which is put before it. [Translator's note: the numbering "first/second" is not stated explicitly in the source; the text proceeds to "the third".] An objection may be raised against the first: that a maṣdar confirming the content of a clause does not come before it, so likewise it does not come in the middle. This is open to consideration, admitting both permission and prohibition, and it is closer to permission.
The third: it is in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial). In the second reading it is nominative as a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is the preposition-phrase before it; «الحُسْنى» is annexed to it (muḍāf ilayhi). What is meant by al-ḥusnā is Paradise; it was also said: the good deed.
The fourth: its accusative is by way of tafsīr (explanation); al-Farrāʾ said this, meaning tamyīz (specification). It is far-fetched.
Ibn ʿAbbās and Masrūq read it accusative and in iḍāfa. There are two explanations of this. One: the mubtadaʾ is omitted, and it is what governs «جزاءَ الحسنى», the implied form being: "so his is the reward, the reward of the best". [Translator's note: an accusative governed by an omitted mubtadaʾ is as written; the sense is that the accusative is governed by the implied maṣdar.] The second: the tanwīn was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, as in the poet's saying:
319 - 6-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا ذاكرَ اللهَ إلاَّ قليلا
(… nor one remembering Allah except a little.)
Al-Mahdawī mentioned it.
ʿAbd Allāh and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read «جزاءٌ» nominative with tanwīn, as a mubtadaʾ; and «الحُسْنى» is a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or accusative by an implied «أَعْني» ("I mean"), or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ.
«يُسْراً» is the naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. a saying having ease. Abū Jaʿfar read «اليُسُر» with ḍamma [on the sīn] wherever it occurs.

semin-durr:90-90.t: His saying: {مَطْلِعَ}: the generality of readers read it with kasra on the lām, while the imperfect is يَطْلُع with ḍamma; so analogy would require fatḥa on the lām in the mafʿal [noun of place] absolutely. But it is one of a group of sister-words in which kasra was heard, though their analogy is fatḥa. [The fatḥa] was read by Ibn al-Ḥasan, ʿĪsā and Ibn Muḥayṣin, and it was transmitted from Ibn Kathīr and the people of Mecca. [Translator's note: as written, «مطلع» with kasra is attributed to "the generality", and the readers here are named without the vowel they read; the reading of the named readers is presumably «مطلَع» with fatḥa. The name «ابن الحسن» is probably «الحسن».] Al-Kisāʾī said: "This dialect has died," meaning: with kasra on the lām in the imperfect and in the mafʿil. This indicates that among the Arabs there were those who said طَلَع يَطْلِعُ with kasra in the imperfect.

semin-durr:91-91.t:
His saying: {كَذَلِكَ}: the kāf is either in the position of the nominative, i.e. "the matter is thus", or in the position of the accusative, i.e. "We did the like of that".
His saying: {بَلَغَ بَيْنَ السَّدَّيْنِ}: «بين» here may be a ẓarf (adverb), with the object omitted, i.e. he attained his aim and purpose; or it may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) by extension of usage, i.e. he reached the place that separates them. [Translator's note: printed «طرفاً»; read as «ظرفاً».]
Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read the sīn of «السَّدَّين» and «سَدَّا» in this sūra with fatḥa; Ḥafṣ read all with fatḥa, I mean the two places in this sūra and the two places in Sūrat Yā Sīn. The two brothers read with fatḥa in «سَدَّاً» in its two sūras and with ḍamma in «السُّدَّيْن». The rest read with ḍamma in all. It was said: they have one meaning. It was also said: the one with ḍamma is what is of the making of Allah the Exalted, and the one with fatḥa is what is of the making of people. This is transmitted from ʿIkrima, al-Kisāʾī and Abū ʿUbayd. It is rejected on the grounds that the two barriers in this sūra are two mountains between which Dhū al-Qarnayn built a barrier; so they are of Allah's making, while the barrier which Dhū al-Qarnayn made is of a creature's making. And «سَدّاً» in Yā Sīn is of the making of Allah the Exalted, because of His saying «وجَعَلْنا»; yet in all of them it was read with fatḥa and ḍamma. So it is known that they are two dialects, like al-ḍaʿf and al-ḍuʿf, and al-faqr and al-fuqr. Al-Khalīl said: the one with ḍamma is a noun, and the one with fatḥa is a maṣdar (verbal noun). This is the preferred view.

semin-durr:93-93.t: His saying: {يَفْقَهُونَ}: the two brothers read it with ḍamma on the yāʾ and kasra on the qāf, from أَفْقَهَ غيرَه (he made another understand); so the object is omitted, i.e. they cannot make others understand speech. [Translator's note: printed «أَقْفَهَ»; read as «أَفْقَهَ».] The rest read with fatḥa, i.e. they do not understand the speech of others, and this has the same meaning as the first. It was also said: they are not necessarily linked, since a person may understand another's speech while the other does not understand his speech, and vice versa.

semin-durr:94-94.t:
His saying: {يَأْجُوجَ وَمَأْجُوجَ}: ʿĀṣim read them with a quiescent hamza, and the rest with a pure alif. There is disagreement about this. It was said: they are both foreign, with no derivation, and they are diptotes because of being proper names and foreign; and the hamza may be original and the alif a substitute for it, or the reverse, because the Arabs play freely with foreign names. It was also said: rather they are both Arabic, and they disagreed about their derivation. It was said: they are derived from ajīj al-nār, which is the blazing of fire and the intensity of its burning. It was said: from al-ajja, which is mixing, or intense heat. It was said: from al-ajj, which is speed in running; from this is the poet's saying:
319 - 7-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تؤجُّ كما أجَّ الظَّليمُ المُنَفَّرُ
(… she speeds along as the startled male ostrich speeds.)
It was also said: from al-ujāj, which is salty, bitter water. Their patterns are yafʿūl and mafʿūl. This is clear on the reading of ʿĀṣim. As for the reading of the rest, the alif may be a substitute for the quiescent hamza; except that among these [readers] there are those whose principle is not changing the quiescent hamza, and they are the majority; but there is no harm in that. It is also possible that their alifs are both additional, and their pattern is fāʿūl, from يَجَّ and مَجَّ.
It is also possible that ماجوج is from ماج يموج, i.e. it was agitated, from which comes al-mawj (waves); its pattern then is mafʿūl, the origin being مَوْجُوج. Abū Ḥātim said this. It is open to objection in that it claims the changing of a weak letter while it is quiescent; its irregularity is like the irregularity of «طائيّ» as the relative adjective of طيِّئ. On the view that they are Arabic and derived, their being diptotes is because of being proper names and feminine, in the sense of "tribe", as its verification has preceded for you in Sūrat Hūd. The same disagreement and reasoning applies in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ, upon them be peace. The hamza in يَأْجوج ومَأْجوج is the dialect of Banū Asad. Ruʾba and his father al-ʿAjjāj read «آجوج».
His saying: «خَراجاً»: Ibn ʿĀmir read «خَرْجاً» here and in al-Muʾminūn with sukūn on the rāʾ; the two brothers read «خراجاً» and «فَخَراج» in both sūras with alif; the rest read as Ibn ʿĀmir in this sūra and in the first [place] in al-Muʾminūn, and in the second, which is «فَخَراج», as the two brothers. It was said: they have one meaning, like al-nawl and al-nawāl. It was also said: al-kharāj with alif is the tribute levied on land every year, and without alif it means a fee (juʿl), i.e. we give you from our wealth, one time, what you can use to help with that.
Makkī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: "The preferred reading is without the alif, because they only offered to give him one gift for his building it, not that this should be imposed on them every year." It was also said: al-kharj is what is levied on heads, and al-kharāj what is levied on land; one says: "Pay the kharj of your head and the kharāj of your land." Ibn al-Aʿrābī said this. It was also said: al-kharj is more specific and al-kharāj more general; Thaʿlab said this. It was also said: al-kharj is a maṣdar (verbal noun), and al-kharāj is a noun for what is given; then the maṣdar may be applied to the object, like al-khalq meaning "the created". [Translator's note: the quotation from Makkī opens with « but its closing mark is not printed; where it ends is unclear.]

semin-durr:95-95.t: His saying: {مَا مَكَّنِّي}: «ما» means "that which". Ibn Kathīr read «مكَّنني» with the nūn pronounced distinctly; the rest with it assimilated into the nūn of protection (nūn al-wiqāya) for lightness.

semin-durr:96-96.t:
His saying: {آتُونِي}: Abū Bakr read «ايتوني» with the connecting hamza (hamzat al-waṣl), from أتى يَأتي, in both places of this sūra, with variation from him in the second. Ḥamza agreed with him in the second without any variation from him. The rest read with the cutting hamza in both.
So «زُبُرَ», on the reading with the connecting hamza, is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "bring me pieces of iron". On the reading with the cutting hamza, it is the second object, because [the verb] becomes transitive to two objects by the hamza. On Abū Bakr's reading the tanwīn of «رَدْماً» has to take kasra because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, since the connecting hamza drops in continuous reading; so it is read for him with kasra on the tanwīn, followed by a quiescent hamza, which is the first radical (fāʾ) of the word. When you begin with the word «ائتوني» in his reading and that of Ḥamza, you begin with a hamza with kasra for connecting, then a pure yāʾ, which is a substitute for the hamza that is the first radical; in continuous reading the connecting hamza drops, so the [radical] hamza returns because the cause of its substitution has gone.
The rest begin and connect with a hamza with fatḥa, because it is a cutting hamza, and they leave the tanwīn of «رَدْماً» quiescent as it is. All this is clear to the grammarians and hidden from the readers.
Al-zubar is the plural of zubra, like ghurfa and ghuraf. Al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma on the bāʾ.
His saying: «ساوَى»: this is the reading of the majority; Qatāda read «سوَّى» with doubling, and ʿĀṣim in one transmission «سُوِّيَ», passive.
His saying: «الصَّدَفَيْن»: Abū Bakr read it with ḍamma on the ṣād and sukūn on the dāl; Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir with ḍamma on both; the rest with fatḥa on both. These are dialects that were read in the Seven. Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and Ḥumayd [read] with fatḥa and sukūn; al-Mājishūn with fatḥa and ḍamma; and ʿĀṣim in one transmission the reverse.
Al-ṣadafān: the two sides of the two mountains. It was also said: [it is] when two mountains face each other with a road between them; the two sides are ṣadafān because they face and meet each other, from صادَفْتُ الرجلَ, i.e. I met him and faced him. Abū ʿUbayd said: "Al-ṣadaf is every high structure, and it is not well-known; the fatḥa is the dialect of Tamīm and the ḍamma the dialect of Ḥimyar."
His saying: «قِطْراً»: it is the word contended for [by two governing verbs]. This verse is the most famous of the grammarians' examples in the chapter of tanāzuʿ (contention of two governors), and it is of giving government to the second, with omission from the first. Al-qiṭr: molten copper or lead.

semin-durr:97-97.t:
His saying: {فَمَا اسطاعوا}: Ḥamza read it with doubling of the ṭāʾ, and the rest without doubling. The rationale for the assimilation is as Abū ʿAlī said: "Since it was not possible to throw the vowel of the tāʾ onto the sīn, lest something be vowelled that is not vowelled" — meaning that the sīn of istafʿala does not take a vowel — "it was assimilated together with the quiescent letter, even though it is not a soft letter. The readers have read more than one word of this kind. Sībawayh recited «ومَسْحِي»," meaning in the poet's saying:
319 - 8- كأنَّه بعد كَلالِ الزَّاجِرِ ... ومَسْحِي مَرُّ عُقُابٍ كاسِرِ
(As though it, after the driver's weariness and my urging, were the swoop of an eagle diving down.)
He means «ومَسْحِه»; he assimilated the ḥāʾ into the hāʾ after changing the hāʾ into ḥāʾ, which is the reverse of the rule of assimilation between close letters. This reading has been judged erroneous (laḥn) by some grammarians. Al-Zajjāj said: "Whoever reads thus is in error and mistaken." Abū ʿAlī said: "It is not permissible."
Al-Aʿshā, from Abū Bakr, read «اصْطاعوا», replacing the sīn with ṣād. Al-Aʿmash read «استطاعوا», like the second.

semin-durr:98-98.t:
His saying: {جَعَلَهُ دَكَّآءَ}: the apparent sense is that al-jaʿl here means "making into", so «دَكَّاء» is a second object. Ibn ʿAṭiyya allowed it to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), with «جعل» meaning "created"; but this is far-fetched, because it [the barrier] already exists at that point. The readers' disagreement on «دَكَّاء» has preceded in al-Aʿrāf.
His saying: {وَعْدُ رَبِّي}: al-waʿd here is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "what is promised", or [it is] in its proper sense.

semin-durr:99-99.t:
His saying: {يَمُوجُ}: a second object of «تَرَكْنا»; the pronoun in «بعضَهم» refers back to «يَأْجُوج ومَأْجوج» or to all of creation.
His saying: «يومئذ»: the tanwīn is a substitute for an omitted clause, its implied form being: "on the day when the promise of my Lord comes", or "when the barrier blocks [them] between them".

semin-durr:101-101.t: His saying: {الذين كَانَتْ}: it may be genitive as a badal (substitute) from «للكافرين», or as ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), or as a naʿt (adjective); it may be accusative by an implied «أَذُمُّ» ("I censure"); and it may be nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ.

semin-durr:102-102.t:
His saying: {أَفَحَسِبَ}: the generality of readers read it with kasra on the sīn and fatḥa on the bāʾ, as a past verb, and {أَن يَتَّخِذُواْ} stands in place of the two objects. The Commander of the Believers ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, Zayd [ibn] ʿAlī, Ibn Kathīr and Yaḥyā ibn Yaʿmar, among others, read it with sukūn on the sīn and ḍamma on the bāʾ, as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being «أَنْ» and what is in its domain. [Translator's note: «زيد علي» as printed; presumably Zayd ibn ʿAlī. Ibn Kathīr here is probably not the canonical reader, whose reading is «أفحسِب» — the source does not specify.]
Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or [it is] on the pattern of verb and agent, because the active participle, when it rests on the hamza [of interrogation], is equal to the verb, as in your saying «أقائمٌ الزيدان»; and it is a sound, good reading."
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: What appears is that this iʿrāb is not permissible, because «حَسْب» is not an active participle that it should govern; and the explanation of one thing by another does not entail that its rules apply to it. Sībawayh mentioned certain adjectives that are treated like nouns, and that the correct way with them is the nominative. Then he said: That is like: مررتُ برجلٍ خيرٌ [منه] أبوه, and مررتُ برجلٍ سواءٌ عليه الخيرُ والشرُّ, and مررت برجلٍ أبٌ له صاحبُه, and مررت برجلٍ حَسْبُك مِنْ رجلٍ هو, and مررت برجلٍ أيُّما رجلٍ هو. Then the Shaykh said: "It is not far-fetched that an overt noun be made nominative by it; they permitted in «مررت برجلٍ أبي عشرةٍ أبوه» that «أبوه» be nominative by «أبي عشرة», because it has the meaning of 'father of ten'."
His saying: «نزلاً»: there are several views on it. The first: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), the plural of «نازِل», like شارِف and شُرُف. The second: it is a noun for the place of alighting. The third: it is a noun for what is prepared for guests who alight, by way of mockery of them, as in the saying of the Exalted: {فَبَشِّرْهُم بِعَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ} [Āl ʿImrān: 21], and the poet's saying:
319 - 9-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تحيَّةُ بينِهم ضَرْبٌ وجميعُ
(… the greeting among them is a blow and …) [Translator's note: the end of the verse is printed «وجميعُ», which looks corrupted (the familiar verse ends «ضربٌ وجيعُ», "a painful blow"); glossed as far as the text allows.]
On these two views its accusative is as a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), i.e. "We made [it]".
Abū Ḥaywa read «نُزْلاً» with sukūn on the zāy, which is a lightening of the well-known [reading].

semin-durr:103-103.t: His saying: {أَعْمَالاً}: a tamyīz (specification) of «الأَخْسَرين»; it is put in the plural because of the difference of kinds.

semin-durr:104-104.t:
His saying: {الذين ضَلَّ}: in it the genitive is permissible as a naʿt (adjective), badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition); the accusative as censure; and the nominative as the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ.
His saying: {يَحْسَبُونَ أَنَّهُمْ يُحْسِنُونَ}: in [the science of] badīʿ this is called "tajnīs al-taṣḥīf" (paronomasia by change of dots) and tajnīs al-khaṭṭ (paronomasia of script), and this is among its best. Al-Buḥturī said:
320 - 0- ولم يكن المُغْتَرُّ بالله إذ شَرَى ... لِيُعْجِزَ والمُعْتَزُّ بالله طالبُهْ
(The one deluded about Allah, when he rebelled, could not escape while al-Muʿtazz bi-llāh was pursuing him.)
The first is from ghurūr (delusion) and the second from ʿizz (might). Among the best of what has come in tajnīs al-taṣḥīf is the saying:
320 - 1- سَقَيْنَني رِيِّيْ وغَنِّيْنَنِيْ ... يُحْتُ بحبِّي حين بِنَّ الخُرُدْ
(They gave me drink to quench my thirst and sang to me; I revealed my love when the maidens departed.)
It is turned by changing the dots into something like:
320 - 2- شَقَيْتَني ربي وعَنَّيْتِنيْ ... بحُبِّ يحيى خَتَنِ ابن الجُرُدْ
(You have made me wretched, my Lord, and you have troubled me with the love of Yaḥyā, the in-law of Ibn al-Jurud.) [Translator's note: these verses are word-play by dot-change and the printed text seems partly corrupted; the glosses are approximate.]
And in one of the letters of the eloquent: «قَبَّلَ قبلَ يَدِكَ ثَراك، عبدٌ عند رَخاك رجاك، آمِلٌ أَمَّك» (Before your hand, he kissed the earth near you — a servant who, at your ease, hoped in you, a hopeful one who made for you).

semin-durr:105-105.t: Ibn ʿAbbās read «فَحَبِطَتْ» with fatḥa on the bāʾ. [Translator's note: the word is printed with kasra on the bāʾ, while the text says fatḥa; i.e. «فحبَطت» is meant.] The generality of readers read «نُقيم» with the nūn of majesty, from «أقام». Mujāhid and ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr [read] «فلا يُقيم» with the yāʾ of the absent [third person], because His saying {بِآيَاتِ رَبِّهِمْ} came before, so the pronoun refers back to it. Mujāhid also [read] «فلا يقومُ لهم», the imperfect of قام, with «وزنٌ» nominative. From ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr also [comes] «فلا يقومُ وزناً» with the accusative, as though he imagined that «قام» is transitive. So said the Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān]. Better than this is to parse this reading as Abū al-Baqāʾ said: the fāʿil (agent) of «يقومُ» is made to be their deeds or their striving, and «وَزْناً» is then accusative in one of two ways: either as a ḥāl (circumstantial) or as a tamyīz (specification).

semin-durr:106-106.t:
His saying: {ذَلِكَ جَزَآؤُهُمْ جَهَنَّمُ}: there are many views on it. The first: «ذلك» is the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "the matter is that", and «جزاؤُهم جهنَّم» is a clause on its own. The second: «ذلك» is a first mubtadaʾ, «جزاؤهم» a second mubtadaʾ and «جهنمُ» its khabar, and it with its khabar is the khabar of the first; the referent (ʿāʾid) is omitted, i.e. "their reward for it". So said Abū al-Baqāʾ; the hāʾ in «به» refers back to «ذلك», and «ذلك» points to the not setting up of a weight.
The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "This explanation needs consideration." I say: if he means consideration from the standpoint of the craft [of grammar], that is granted. The point of consideration is that the referent has been omitted without anything permitting it except by strain: for the referent to the mubtadaʾ, when it is genitive, is only omitted if it is governed by a preposition of partition or of place, or if it governs [sic] a referent governed before it by a preposition with which the omitted one was governed, as in the poet's saying:
320 - 2- أَصِخْ فالذي تُدْعَى به أنت مُفْلِحٌ ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Listen! For by what you are called to, you are successful …)
i.e. "successful by it". [Translator's note: the condition is stated awkwardly in the source («أو يَجُرُّ عائداً جُرَّ قبله بحرفٍ، جُرَّ به المحذوفُ»); the intended sense is: or when the relative pronoun's referent is governed by the same preposition that governs something before it.] If he means from the standpoint of meaning, then it is a good meaning.
The third: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, «جزاؤهم» a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), and «جهنم» its khabar. The fourth: «ذلك» is also a mubtadaʾ, «جزاؤهم» its khabar, and «جهنمُ» a badal or bayān, or the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ. The fifth: «ذلك» is made a mubtadaʾ, «جزاؤهم» a badal or bayān, «جهنم» the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ, and «بما كفروا» the khabar of the first, the clause being parenthetical. The sixth: «ذلك» is a mubtadaʾ, the preposition-phrase is the khabar, and «جزاؤهم جهنمُ» is a parenthetical clause; this is far-fetched. The seventh: «ذلك» points to a group — they are mentioned in His saying «بالأخسرين» — and the plural is pointed to as the singular is pointed to, as though it were said: "those, their reward is Hell"; and the preceding iʿrāb applies to this implied form.
His saying: «واتَّخذوا»: there are two views on it. The first: it is conjoined to «كفروا», so its position is nominative, since it is conjoined to the khabar of «إنَّ». [Translator's note: as written; «كفروا» here is in the ṣila of «ما» in «بما كفروا», not the khabar of «إنَّ» — translated as it stands.] The second: it is resumptive, so it has no grammatical position.
The bāʾ in His saying «بما كفروا» may not be attached to «جزاؤهم», because of the separation between the maṣdar (verbal noun) and what it governs.

semin-durr:107-107.t: His saying: {نُزُلاً}: in it is what has preceded: its being a noun for the place of alighting, or what is prepared for a guest. In its accusative there are two views. The first: it is the khabar (predicate) of «كانت», and «لهم» is attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «نُزُلا», or by way of clarification (bayān), or [attached] to «كانت» according to whoever holds that view. The second: it is a ḥāl from «جنات», i.e. "having hospitality", and the khabar is the preposition-phrase.

semin-durr:108-108.t:
His saying: {لاَ يَبْغُونَ}: the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial), either from the one to whom «خالدين» refers, or from the pronoun in «خالدين», so it is an overlapping (mutadākhila) ḥāl.
Al-ḥiwal: it was said that it is a maṣdar (verbal noun) meaning "changing place"; one says حال عن مكانه حِوَلاً, so it is a maṣdar like al-ʿiwaj, al-ʿiwad and al-ṣighar. The poet said:
320 - 4- لكلِّ دولةٍ أجلُ ... ثم يُتاحُ لها حِوَل
(Every dynasty has a term, then a change is decreed for it.)
Al-Zajjāj said: "According to some, it means a stratagem for moving." Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Al-ḥiwal means changing place; Mujāhid said: 'a place to move to'." He recited the preceding rajaz, then said: "It is as though it is a collective noun, as though its singular is ḥawāla." I say: this is strange; the well-known view is the first. Keeping the weak letter sound in fiʿal is the common case if it is a singular, like al-ḥiwal; if it is a plural then the reverse, like «ثِيَرة» and . . . . [Translator's note: the text breaks off here in the source.]

semin-durr:109-109.t:
His saying: {تَنفَدَ}: the two brothers read «يَنْفَذَ» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, because the feminine is figurative; the rest with the upper-dotted tāʾ because of the feminine form of the word. [Translator's note: printed «يَنْفَذَ» with dhāl; read as «يَنْفَدَ».] Al-Sulamī read — and it was transmitted from Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim — «تَنَفَّدَ» with doubling of the fāʾ; it is the reflexive (muṭāwiʿ) of نَفَّدَ with doubling, as in "I broke it and it broke apart" (كسَّرته فتكسَّر). The reading of the rest is the reflexive of أَنْفَدْته.
His saying: «ولو جِئنا»: its answer is omitted because the meaning is understood, its implied form being: "it would be exhausted". The generality of readers read «مَدَداً» with fatḥa on the mīm; al-Aʿmash read it with kasra; its accusative is as tamyīz (specification), as in the poet's saying:
320 - 5-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فإنَّ الهوى يَكْفِيْكه مثلُه صَبْرا
(… for passion — its like in patience suffices you against it.)
Ibn Masʿūd and Ibn ʿAbbās read «مِداداً», like the first. Its accusative is also as tamyīz according to Abū al-Baqāʾ. Others — like Abū al-Faḍl al-Rāzī — said: it is accusative as a maṣdar meaning al-imdād (supplying), like {أَنبَتَكُمْ مِّنَ الأرض نَبَاتاً} [Nūḥ: 17]. He said: the meaning is: "even if We supplied it with its like, a supplying."

semin-durr:110-110.t:
His saying: {أَنَّمَآ إلهكم}: this «أنَّ» is maṣdariyya (forming a verbal noun), even though it is restrained by «ما». This maṣdar stands in place of the agent (nāʾib fāʿil, deputy agent), as though it were said: "only the Oneness [of Allah] is revealed to me".
His saying: {وَلاَ يُشْرِكْ}: the generality of readers read it with the lower-dotted yāʾ, conjoining it to a command. It was transmitted from Abū ʿAmr {وَلاَ تُشْرِكْ} with the upper-dotted tāʾ, as address, by way of iltifāt (shift) from the absent [third person] to address; then in His saying {بِعِبَادَةِ رَبِّهِ} there is a shift back to the first. Had it come according to the second shift, it would have been said "your Lord". The bāʾ is causal, i.e. "because of"; it was also said: it means "in".
Al-firdaws: a garden of grapevines specifically. It was also said: rather, one which is mostly grapevines. It was also said: everything enclosed is a firdaws; the plural is farādīs. Al-Mubarrad said: "Al-firdaws, according to what I heard from the Arabs, is dense, intertwined trees, and mostly it is of grapes." Al-Zajjāj reported that they are the valleys that grow various kinds of plants. There is disagreement about it: it was said that it is Arabic, and it was said foreign — and is it Greek (Rūmī), Persian or Syriac? It was said that it was not heard in the speech of the Arabs except in a verse of Ḥassān:
320 - 6- وإنَّ ثوابَ اللهِ كلَّ مُوحِّدِ ... جِنانٌ من الفردوسِ فيها يُخْلَّدُ
(The reward of Allah for every monotheist is gardens of Firdaws in which he is made eternal.)
This is not correct, because it was heard in the poetry of Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt:
320 - 7- كانت منازلُهمْ إذ ذاك ظاهرةً ... فيها الفَراديسُ ثم الثومُ والبَصَلُ
(Their dwellings were then plain to see, in them gardens, then garlic and onions.)
One says كَرْمٌ مُفَرْدَسٌ, i.e. trellised; for this reason the meadow below al-Yamāma was called firdaws.
The annexation of «جنَّات» to al-firdaws is an annexation of clarification (iḍāfat tabyīn).
[Translator's note: the discussion of al-firdaws relates to verse 107 ({جَنَّاتُ الفردوس}); it is found here in the source entry.]

semin-durr:1-1.t: His words: {وَلَمْ يَجْعَل}: there are several views on this clause. First: that it is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the ṣila (relative clause) before it. Second: that it is parenthetical between the ḥāl (circumstantial), namely «قَيِّماً», and its owner, namely «الكتابَ». Third: that it is a ḥāl of «الكتابَ». The treatment of «قَيِّماً» depends on these views.

semin-durr:2-2.t:
His words: {قَيِّماً}: there are several views on it. First: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «الكتاب», and the clause in His words «ولم يَجْعَلْ» is parenthetical between them. Al-Zamakhsharī forbade this, saying: "If you say: by what is «قَيِّماً» accusative? I say: the best is that it be accusative by an implied [verb]; it was not made a ḥāl of «الكتابَ» because His words «ولم يَجْعَلْ» are conjoined to «أَنْزَلَ», so it falls within the domain of the ṣila (relative clause); whoever makes it a ḥāl separates the ḥāl from its owner by part of the ṣila." Abū al-Baqāʾ said likewise. The answer to this is what was stated above: that the clause is parenthetical, not conjoined to the ṣila.
Second: that it is a ḥāl of the hāʾ in «له». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The ḥāl is emphatic (muʾakkida); and it is said: transitory (muntaqila)." I say: the view that it is transitory is not valid.
Third: that it is accusative by an implied verb, its implied form being "He made it upright". Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Its implied form is: and He did not put in it any crookedness, He made it upright; because when He negated crookedness of it, He affirmed uprightness for it." He said: "If you say: what is the benefit of combining the negation of crookedness and the affirmation of uprightness, when either one suffices for the other? I say: its benefit is emphasis; for many an upright thing, attested as upright, is not free of the slightest crookedness upon probing and scrutiny."
Fourth: that it is a second ḥāl, the negated clause before it also being a ḥāl, and multiple ḥāls for a single owner are permitted. The implied form: "He sent it down, not putting any crookedness in it, upright."
Fifth: that it is also a ḥāl, but it is a badal (substitute) of the clause before it, since that is a ḥāl, and substituting a single word for a clause, when the clause is equivalent to a single word, is permitted. The implied form: … And this is just as [Translator's note: the text has «كنا», read as «كما»] the clause was substituted for the single word in their saying «عَرَفْتُ زيداً أبو مَنْ هو» ("I knew Zayd — whose father he is"). [Translator's note: after «والتقديرُ» no implied form is given in the text.]
There are two views on the pronoun in «له». First: that it is for the Book, and the preceding analyses are based on this. Second: that it refers to «عبدِه», and this is not clear.
The majority read with the yāʾ doubled. Abān ibn Taghlib read it with fatḥa, undoubled [قَيَماً]. The discussion of it was given earlier.
Ḥafṣ paused on the tanwīn of «عِوَجاً», changing it into an alif, [and made] a slight silence (sakta) without breaking breath, to indicate that «قَيِّماً» is not connected with «عِوَجاً» but is among the attributes of the Book. The others paid no heed to this misconception and did not make the silence, relying on the understanding of the meaning.
I say: what Ḥafṣ did may be supported by what is in some of the Companions' codices: «ولم يَجْعَلْ له عِوَجاً، لكنْ جَعَلَه قيَّماً» ("and He did not put in it any crookedness, but made it upright"). Some of the reciters state it without qualification, saying "he pauses on «عِوَجا»", and do not say "he changes the tanwīn into an alif"; so that is possible, and it is closer to his purpose as I mentioned.
I saw that Shaykh Shihāb al-Dīn Abū Shāma transmitted this — I mean the unqualified statement — from Ibn Ghalbūn and Abū ʿAlī al-Ahwāzī. Then he said: "There is reservation about that — i.e. about changing the tanwīn into an alif — for had he paused on the tanwīn, it would have better indicated his purpose, namely that he is pausing with the intention of continuing." End of quotation.
Al-Ahwāzī said: "It is not a preferred pause, because in the speech there is fronting and postponing, its meaning being: He sent down upon His servant the Book upright, and did not put in it any crookedness." I say: the claim of fronting and postponing, though others have held it, is rejected because it is contrary to the default; its precise treatment was given earlier.
Ḥafṣ did in several places of the Qurʾān the like of what he did here, namely a slight silence that removes a damaging misconception. Among them: he used to pause on «مَرْقَدِنا» and begin {هَذَا مَا وَعَدَ الرحمن} [Yā Sīn: 52]. He said: "So that it should not be imagined that «هذا» is an adjective of «مَرْقَدِنا»; the pause shows that the disbelievers' speech has ended, and then the speech/ of others begins." It is said: they are the angels; it is said: they are the believers. In Yā Sīn there will come what requires «هذا» to be an adjective of «مَرْقَدِنا», so that [purpose] would be lost.
Among them: {وَقِيلَ مَنْ رَاقٍ} [al-Qiyāma: 27]. He used to pause on the nūn of «مَنْ» and begin «راقٍ». He said: so that it should not be imagined that it is a single word on the pattern faʿʿāl, an intensive active participle from مَرَق يَمْرُق, i.e. marrāq.
Among them: {بَلْ رَانَ} [al-Muṭaffifīn: 14]: he used to pause on the lām of «بل» and begin «رانَ», for the reason given above.
Al-Mahdawī said: "The like of that should have been binding on Ḥafṣ in what resembles these places, and he does not do it; so his reading has no ground of argument except following what is transmitted in the narration." Abū Shāma said: "More deserving than these places of attention to pausing are: «ولا يَحْزُنْكَ قولُهم. {إِنَّ العزة للَّهِ جَمِيعاً}» [Yūnus: 65] — the pause being on «قَوْلُهم», so that it should not be imagined that what follows is what they say — and likewise {أَنَّهُمْ أَصْحَابُ النار * الذين يَحْمِلُونَ العرش} [Ghāfir: 6–7]: care should be taken to pause on «النار», so that the adjective [relation] should not be imagined."
[Translator's note: the source gives the reference as [غافر: 67]; the two verses are Ghāfir 6–7.]
I say: imagining these things is the most far-fetched of the far-fetched. Abū Shāma also said: "If pausing on the lām and the nūn so that they appear were necessary, it would be necessary in every assimilated [letter]." I say: he means in «بَلْ رَان» and in «مَنْ راقٍ».
His words: «لِيُنْذِرَ»: there are two views on this lām. First: that it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «قَيِّماً»; al-Ḥawfī said this. Second — and it is the apparent view — that it is attached to «أَنْزَلَ». The fāʿil (agent) of «لِيُنْذِرَ» may be «الكتابَ», or Allah, or the Messenger.
«أَنْذَرَ» takes two objects: {إِنَّآ أَنذَرْنَاكُمْ عَذَاباً قَرِيباً} [al-Nabaʾ: 40], {فَقُلْ أَنذَرْتُكُمْ صَاعِقَةً} [Fuṣṣilat: 13]. Its first object is omitted; al-Zamakhsharī gave its implied form as "to warn those who disbelieved", and others as "to warn the servants", or "to warn you", or "to warn the world". His implied form is better, because it is the counterpart of His words {وَيُبَشِّرَ المؤمنين}, and they are their opposite.
And just as He omitted the one warned and brought the thing warned of here, He omitted the thing warned of and brought the one warned in His words {وَيُنْذِرَ الذين قَالُواْ} [al-Kahf: 4]; so He omitted the first [object] from the first [verb] because what is in the second indicates it, and the second from the second because what is in the first indicates it; and this is the utmost of eloquence. And since the glad tidings were not repeated, He mentioned both its objects, saying: {وَيُبَشِّرَ المؤمنين الذين يَعْمَلُونَ الصالحات أَنَّ لَهُمْ أَجْراً}.
[Translator's note: «وكما حَذَفَ المُنْذِرُ» in the text is to be understood as «المُنْذَرَ» (the one warned), as the following sentence shows.]
His words: {مِّن لَّدُنْهُ}: Abū Bakr from ʿĀṣim read with sukūn on the dāl with ishmām (lip-rounding hint) of ḍamma, and kasra on the nūn and on the hāʾ, joined to a yāʾ; so he reads «مِنْ لَدْنِهِيْ». The rest read ḍamma on the dāl, sukūn on [the nūn] and ḍamma on the hāʾ, and they follow their rules regarding it: Ibn Kathīr joins it with a wāw, as in minhū and ʿanhū, and the others do not join it with anything.
The explanation of Abū Bakr's reading: he made the dāl quiescent for lightening, like making the middle radical of «عَضُد» quiescent, while the nūn is quiescent; so two quiescent letters met, and he gave the nūn kasra because of the meeting of two quiescents. By right he should have given kasra to the first, according to the well-known rule, except that this would entail returning to what he fled from. An explanation verifying this will come at His words {وَيَخْشَ الله وَيَتَّقْهِ} [verse 52] in Sūrat al-Nūr, and we will speak about it there. When he gave the nūn kasra for the reason I mentioned to you, he gave the hāʾ kasra by harmony, according to his rule, and joined it with a yāʾ. And he gave the dāl ishmām as an indication of its original vowel.
Ishmām here means rounding the lips without pronouncing, and for this reason the sighted, not the blind, perceive it. This is how the reciters have established it, and there is reservation about it, because the ishmām referred to is realised only when pausing at the end of the word, so it is suitable only as an indication of the vowel of the final letter when it is nominative and paused on, as in «جاء الرجل»; this is how the grammarians mentioned it. As for its being produced in the middle of a word, that is inconceivable unless the speaker pauses on that quiescent letter and then pronounces the rest of the word. If you test your pronunciation of this noble word, you will find the matter so: you do not pronounce the dāl quiescent while indicating its ḍamma unless you pause on it and then produce the rest of the word.
If you say: I produce the indication of the ḍamma only after finishing the whole word — it will be said to you: then the indication specifying the letter whose vowel is being pointed to is lost. This may be answered by saying that there is nothing in the word whose vowel could be pointed to except the dāl. It was stated earlier in "Yūsuf" that, regarding the ishmām in {لاَ تَأْمَنَّا} [verse 11], when we interpret it as pointing to the ḍamma, some do it before the assimilation is complete and some after it; this is its like. It was also stated earlier that ishmām is used for four meanings, whose precise treatment was given.
{مِّن لَّدُنْهُ} is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «لِيُنْذِرَ»/. It may be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «بَأْساً», and it may be a ḥāl of the pronoun in «شديداً».
It was also read «ويُبَشِّرُ» in the nominative, as resumptive.

semin-durr:3-3.t:
His words: {مَّاكِثِينَ}: a ḥāl (circumstantial), either of the genitive pronoun in «لهم», or of the nominative pronoun latent in it, or of «أجراً», since it is specified by the adjective — except that this last comes only on the view of the Kufans, for they do not require the pronoun to appear overtly in an adjective applied to other than the one it belongs to, when ambiguity is safe; had it been a ḥāl of it according to the Basrans, He would have said: «ماكثين هم فيه». On the Kufan view, it may also be a second adjective of «أَجْراً». Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "It is said: it is an adjective of «أَجْراً», and the referent pronoun is the hāʾ of «فيه»." He did not address the overt appearance of the pronoun or its absence with respect to the two schools.
«أبداً» is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf) by «ماكثين».

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His words: {مَّا لَهُمْ بِهِ}: i.e. of the child, or of His taking [a child], or of the saying indicated by «اتَّخذ» and by «قالوا», or of Allah.
There are three views on this negated clause. The most evident: that it is resumptive, brought to report that. Second: that it is an adjective of «الولد»; al-Mahdawī said this. Ibn ʿAṭiyya rejected it: only the speakers would describe it thus, and they did not intend to describe it thus. Third: that it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of «قالوا», i.e. "they said it, being ignorant".
{مِنْ عِلْمٍ} may be a fāʿil (agent), the preposition-phrase being what makes it nominative; or a mubtadaʾ (subject), the preposition-phrase being the khabar (predicate). «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida) on both views.
His words: {كَبُرَتْ كَلِمَةً}: there are two views on the fāʿil of «كَبُرَتْ». First: that it is a latent pronoun referring to their statement understood from His words «قالوا: اتَّخذ الله», i.e. "their statement is grave"; «كلمةً» is accusative as a tamyīz (specification), and the sense of the speech is exclamation, i.e. "how grave it is as a word!". The clause «تَخْرُجُ» is an adjective of «كلمة». Its being declared enormous indicates [that it is so], because some of what occurs to the mind a person does not dare to express in words.
Second: that the fāʿil is a latent pronoun explained by the indefinite noun after it, accusative as a tamyīz, and its meaning is blame, like «بِئس رجلاً» ("how bad a man!"). On this view, the specified object of blame (al-makhṣūṣ bi-l-dhamm) is omitted, its implied form being: "how grave it is as a word — a word coming out of their mouths — that hideous statement".
The majority read «كلمةً» in the accusative, and there are two views on it: accusative as a tamyīz, whose precise treatment was given in the two preceding views; and second, accusative as a ḥāl, which is not evident.
His words: «تَخْرُجُ»: there are two views on the clause. First: it is an adjective of «كلمة». Second: that it is an adjective of the implied specified object of blame, its implied form being: "how grave, as a word, is a word coming out".
Al-Ḥasan, Ibn Muḥayṣin, Ibn Yaʿmar and Ibn Kathīr — in the narration of al-Qawwās from him — read «كلمةٌ» in the nominative as fāʿil, «وتَخْرُج» also being an adjective of it. It was also read «كَبْرَتْ» with sukūn on the bāʾ, which is the dialect of Tamīm.
His words: «كَذِباً»: there are two views on it. First: it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), because it includes the meaning of a clause. Second: it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "a false saying".

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His words: {إِن لَّمْ يُؤْمِنُواْ}: the majority read «إنْ» with kasra, as conditional; according to the majority [of grammarians] the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted because His words «فَلَعَلَّكَ» indicate it, and according to others it is a fronted apodosis. It was also read «أَنْ لم» with fatḥa, with the preposition omitted, i.e. "because they did not believe".
It was also read «باخِعُ نَفْسِكَ» with annexation, the original being the accusative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«باخع نفسك» was read according to the original and with annexation, i.e. killing it and destroying it. It is for the future for those who read «إنْ لم يُؤمنوا», and for the past for those who read «أن لم تُؤْمنوا», meaning 'because they did not believe'." I say: he means that «باخع» is for the future in the reading with kasra on «إنْ», since it is conditional, and for the past in the reading with fatḥa; and that comes only in the reading with annexation, since the past is inconceivable with the accusative according to the Basrans. On this basis it follows that only those who read «باخع» with annexation could read the fatḥa, and that requires transmission and authoritative report.
«ولعلَّك»: it is said: for apprehension, in its basic meaning. It is said: for interrogation, and this is the view of the Kufans. It is said: for prohibition, i.e. "do not destroy [yourself]".
Al-bakhʿ is destroying. One says: بَخَع الرجُل نفسَه يَبْخَعُها بَخْعاً وبُخُوعاً, he destroyed it with grief. Dhū al-Rumma said:
312 - 2- ألا أيُّهذا الباخعُ الوجدُ نفسَه ... لِشَيْءٍ نَحَتْه عن يديه المَقادِرُ
(O you whom grief is destroying [الباخع], over a thing the decrees have removed from his hands.)
He means نَحَّته with doubling, and lightened it./ Al-Aṣmaʿī said: "He used to recite it «الوجدَ» in the accusative as an object of purpose", and Abū ʿUbayda narrated it in the nominative as fāʿil of «الباخع».
It is said: al-bakhʿ is weakening the land by cultivation; al-Kisāʾī said this. It is said: it is exhausting the land; and in the ḥadīth of ʿĀʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, about ʿUmar: «بَخَعَ جَهْدُ الأرضِ» [Translator's note: so in the text], meaning he exhausted it until he took what was in it of the wealth of its kings; and this is a metaphor. Al-Zamakhsharī did not explain it here otherwise than as killing and destroying. In Sūrat al-Shuʿarāʾ he said: "Al-bakhʿ is that the slaughter reaches al-bikhāh [Translator's note: so in the text, «البِخاه»; the word intended in al-Zamakhsharī is البِخاع], with a bāʾ, which is a vein hidden within the vertebrae; and that is the utmost limit of the slaughterer." End of quotation. I heard our shaykh ʿAlāʾ al-Dīn al-Qūnawī say: "I searched through the books of medicine and anatomy and found no basis for it." I say: it is possible that when they mentioned it they called it by another name, being better known among them.
Al-Rāghib said: "Al-bakhʿ is killing oneself out of grief." Then he said: "بَخَعَ فلانٌ بالطاعةِ and بما عليه من الحقِّ: when he acknowledges it and submits with great reluctance — which is like destroying oneself in its severity."
His words: «على آثارِهم»: attached (mutaʿalliq) to «باخعٌ», i.e. after their perishing.
His words: «أَسَفَاً»: it may be a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), governed by «باخعٌ», or a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in «باخعٌ».

semin-durr:7-7.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {زِينَةً}: it may be accusative as an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu), or accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) if you take «جَعَلْنا» to mean "We created"; and it may be a second object if «جَعَلَ» is of transformation (taṣyīr). «لها» is attached (mutaʿalliq) to «زِيْنةً» as a cause; the lām may be redundant (zāʾida) in the object; and it may be attached to an omitted element as an adjective of «زينة».
His words: «لِنَبْلُوَهُمْ»: attached to «جَعَلْنا» in both its meanings.
His words: «أيُّهم أحسنُ»: two views are possible for «أيُّهم». First: that it is interrogative, nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), with «أحسنُ» its khabar (predicate), and the clause in the position of the accusative, suspended (muʿallaqa) by «نَبْلُوَهم», because [testing] is a means of knowing, like asking and looking. Second: that it is a relative meaning «الذي», «أحسنُ» being the khabar of an implied mubtadaʾ and the clause the ṣila (relative clause) of «أيُّهم»; this relative would then be in the position of the accusative as a badal (substitute) of the object of «لنبلوَهم», its implied form being "that We may test the one who is best". In that case the ḍamma in «أيُّهم» may be that of indeclinability (bināʾ), as it is in the words of Allah the Exalted {لَنَنزِعَنَّ مِن كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ} [Maryam: 69] according to one of the opinions, and in his words:
312 - 3- إذا ما أَتَيْتَ بني مالكٍ ... فَسَلِّمْ على أَيُّهم أَفْضَلُ
(When you come to the Banū Mālik, greet whichever of them is the best.)
— the condition for indeclinability being present, namely being annexed in wording and the omission of the head of the ṣila; this is the position of Sībawayh — or it may be declinable, because indeclinability is permitted, not obligatory. Among [instances of] declension is what was read anomalously: {أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرحمن} [Maryam: 69] [i.e. أيَّهم]; the precise treatment of this will come, Allah willing, in Maryam.
The pronoun in «لِنَبْلُوَهم» and «أيُّهم» refers to what is understood from the context, namely the inhabitants of the earth. It is said: it refers to «ما على الأرض» if the rational beings are meant by it. In the exegesis: what is meant by that is the shepherds [i.e. those in charge]; and it is said: the scholars, the righteous and the caliphs.

semin-durr:8-8.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {صَعِيداً}: a second object, because «الجَعْل» here is nothing but transformation (taṣyīr). Al-ṣaʿīd is soil, and al-juruz is that which has no vegetation. One says: "a juzur year" and "ajrāz years": having no rain; "juzur land" and "ajrāz lands": having no vegetation [Translator's note: the text writes «جُزُر» in both expressions; the word under discussion is «جُرُز»]. جَرَزَتِ الأرضُ: when its vegetation has gone through drought or locusts; جَرَز الأرضَ الجرادُ: the locusts ate what was in it. Al-jarūz is the woman who eats a great deal. [The poet] said:
312 - 4- إنَّ العَجوزَ خَبَّةً جَرُوزا ... تأكلُ كلَّ ليلةٍ قَفيزا
(The old woman, a cunning glutton [جروز], eats a qafīz [measure] every night.)

semin-durr:9-9.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَمْ حَسِبْتَ}: this «أم» is the disconnected one (munqaṭiʿa), so it is rendered by «بل» — the one for transition, not cancellation — together with the interrogative hamza according to the majority of grammarians; and by «بل» alone, or by the hamza alone, according to others. The precise treatment of it was given earlier.
«أنَّ» and what is within its domain take the place of the two objects or of one of them, according to the well-known disagreement.
Al-kahf: it is said: any cave whatsoever. It is said: it is what is wide in a mountain; if it is not wide, it is a ghār. Its plural is «كُهوف» for many and «أَكْهُف» for few.
Al-raqīm: it is said: in the sense of marqūm (inscribed). It is said: in the sense of rāqim. It is said: it is the name of the dog belonging to the Companions of the Cave. They cited for Umayya ibn Abī al-Ṣalt:
312 - 5- وليسَ بها إلا الرَّقيمُ مُجاوِراً ... وصِيدَهُمُ، والقومُ بالكهفِ هُمَّدُ
(And none is there but al-Raqīm, keeping close to their threshold, while the people lie motionless in the Cave.)
/His words: «عَجَبا»: it may be the khabar (predicate), with {مِنْ آيَاتِنَا} a ḥāl (circumstantial) of it; or a second khabar, with {مِنْ آيَاتِنَا} the first khabar; or «عجباً» may be a ḥāl of the pronoun latent in {مِنْ آيَاتِنَا}, since it occurs as a khabar. It was made singular, although in meaning it is an adjective of a group, because its origin is the maṣdar (verbal noun). It is said: «عَجَباً» is originally an adjective of an omitted [noun], its implied form being "a wondrous sign". It is said: on [the basis of] omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "a sign possessing wonder".
[Translator's note: the text writes the plural of paucity as «أَكْهَف»; the usual form is «أَكْهُف».]

semin-durr:10-10.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِذْ أَوَى}: it may be accusative by «عَجَباً», or accusative by [an implied] «اذْكُر» (remember).
His words: «وهَيِّئْ»: the majority read with a hamza after the doubled yāʾ. Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and al-Zuhrī read with two yāʾs, the second undoubled, as though he changed the hamza into a yāʾ, even though its quiescence is incidental. It is narrated from ʿĀṣim: «وَهَيَّ» with a doubled yāʾ only. It is possible that he dropped the hamza from the very outset for lightening, or that he changed it as Abū Jaʿfar did and then treated the yāʾ as an original weak letter and dropped it, even though the majority [usage] is otherwise; and of this is:
312 - 6- جَرِيْءٍ متى يُظْلَمْ يعاقِبْ بظُلْمِه ... سريعاً وإلاَّ يُبْدَ بالظلمِ يَظْلمِ
(A bold one: whenever he is wronged he punishes the wrong swiftly, and if he is not first [يُبْدَ] wronged, he wrongs.)
Abū Rajāʾ read «رُشْدا» with ḍamma on the rāʾ and sukūn on the shīn; the precise treatment of that was given in al-Aʿrāf. The reading of the majority here is more fitting, so as to agree with the verse-endings.

semin-durr:11-11.t:
His words: {فَضَرَبْنَا}: its object is omitted, i.e. "We drew the preventing veil". {على آذَانِهِمْ} is a metaphor for the persistence of sleep, as in the words of al-Aswad:
312 - 7- ومن الحوادِث لا أبالَكِ أنني ... ضُرِبَتْ عَلَيَّ الأرضُ بالأَسْدادِ
(Among the misfortunes — may you have no father! — is that the earth has been sealed [ضُربت] upon me with barriers.)
Al-Farazdaq said:
312 - 8- ضَرَبَتْ عليكَ العَنْكَبوتَ بنَسْجِها ... وقَضَى عليك به الكتاب المُنَزَّلُ
(The spider has drawn [ضربت] its web over you, and the revealed Book has decreed it upon you.)
He specified the ears because sleep comes about by drawing [a veil] over them in particular.
And «آذانهم» was inclined (imāla) by … [Note: the text is incomplete here in the source, marked «. . . .».]
«سنينَ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for «ضَرَبْنا». «عَدَداً» may be a maṣdar (verbal noun), or faʿal in the sense of mafʿūl, like al-qabaḍ and al-naqaṣ. On the first, its accusative may be from two angles: as an adjective of «سنين» with an omission, i.e. "possessing number", or by way of hyperbole; or accusative by an implied verb, i.e. "they are counted a counting". On the second: it is an adjective and nothing else, i.e. "counted".

semin-durr:12-12.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {لِنَعْلَمَ}: attached (mutaʿalliq) to the raising [بعثناهم]. The majority read with the nūn of majesty, in keeping with what preceded. Al-Zuhrī read «لِيَعْلم» with the yāʾ of the absent [third person], the fāʿil (agent) being Allah the Exalted; in it is a shift (iltifāt) from the first person to the third. The fāʿil may also be {أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ}, if we make it a relative, as will come.
It was also read «ليُعْلَمَ» in the passive. As for what stands in place of the fāʿil, al-Zamakhsharī said: "The content of the clause, just as it is the object of knowing." The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected this on the ground that it is not the position of the Basrans. The precise treatment of this was given at the beginning of al-Baqara.
The Kufans have, regarding a clause standing in place of the fāʿil or of the deputy agent (nāʾib fāʿil): permission without restriction, and a distinction whereby it is permitted with what is suspended (yuʿallaq), like this verse; so al-Zamakhsharī followed their approach on [both] their views. If we make {أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ} a relative, the verb may also be predicated of it in this reading, just as it could be predicated of it in the reading before it.
It was also read «ليُعْلِمَ» with ḍamma on the yāʾ, the fāʿil being Allah the Exalted and the first object omitted, its implied form being "that Allah may make the people know". {أَيُّ الحِزْبَيْنِ} is then in the position of the second object only, if it is [knowing] of acquaintance (ʿirfāniyya), and in the position of the two objects if it is [knowing] of certainty (yaqīniyya).
His words: «أَحْصَى»: two views are possible. First: that it is an elative of preference (afʿal al-tafḍīl), the khabar (predicate) of «أيُّهم», «أيُّهم» being interrogative; this clause is suspended [in its object relation] by the [verb of] knowing before it. «لِما لَبِثُوا» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أَمَداً», because if it were placed after it, it would be its adjective. The lām may have its basic causal meaning, i.e. "for the sake of … Abū al-Baqāʾ" [Translator's note: the text is defective here: «أي: لأجل أبو البقاء»; something appears to have dropped out, presumably "for the sake of their tarrying; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this"]. It may be redundant (zāʾida), with «ما» an object, either of «أَحْصى» — on the view of those who allow the elative to govern a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) — or of an implied verb. «أمداً» is the object of «لَبِثُوا», or accusative by an implied verb indicated by the elative according to the majority, or accusative by the elative itself according to those who hold that.
The second view: that «أَحْصَى» is a past verb, «أمَداً» its object, and «لِمَا لَبثوا» attached to it, or a ḥāl of «أَمَداً», or the lām in it is redundant; on this last, «أمداً» is accusative by «لبثوا». «ما» is maṣdariyya or means «الذي». Al-Zajjāj and al-Tibrīzī chose the first — I mean «أَحْصى» being elative —/ while Abū ʿAlī [al-Fārisī], al-Zamakhsharī and Ibn ʿAṭiyya chose the second. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: what do you say about one who makes it an elative? I say: it is not the sound view; that is because forming it from a non-triliteral [verb] is not according to analogy, and [expressions] like «أَعْدَى من الجَرَب» ('more infectious than mange') and «أفلس من ابن المُذَلَّق» ('more bankrupt than Ibn al-Mudhallaq') are anomalous; and analogy on the anomalous is forbidden outside the Qurʾān, so how much more in it? And because «أَمَداً» is either accusative by the elative — and the elative does not govern — or accusative by «لبثوا», in which case the meaning is not sound for it. If you claim: I make it accusative by an implied verb, as one was implied in his words:
3129 - . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... وأَضْرَبَ منا بالسيوفِ القَوانِسا
(… and more striking than us, with swords, the helmet-tops [القوانس].)
then you have gone a long way round, since you refused to let [«أحصى»] be a verb and then returned to it out of necessity."
The Shaykh disputed with him, saying: "As for his claim that it is anomalous, the position of Sībawayh is contrary to it. That is because regarding afʿala there are three positions: permission without restriction, attributed to Sībawayh; prohibition without restriction, which is the position of al-Fārisī; and a distinction between its hamza being for transitivity, in which case it is forbidden, and its not being so, in which case it is permitted — and in this [word] the hamza is not for transitivity. As for his saying 'the elative does not govern', it is not correct, because it governs the tamyīz (specification), and «أَمَداً» is a tamyīz, not a mafʿūl bihi, as you say: 'Zayd is the sharpest of people in sword', and 'Zayd is the sharpest at heads in sword'."
I say: what drove al-Zamakhsharī not to make it a tamyīz, despite its being evident at first glance, is the invalidity of its meaning. That is because the condition of the tamyīz in this topic is that the description before it may validly be ascribed to it and it be described by it. Do you not see, in his example "Zayd is the sharpest of people in sword", how it may validly be predicated of it, so that one says "Zayd — his sword cuts", "his sword is sharp", and so on? Here, counting (al-iḥṣāʾ) is not an attribute of the term (al-amad), nor may it validly be ascribed to it; it is only an attribute of the two parties. This is subtle.
The Shaykh had transmitted from Abū al-Baqāʾ its accusative as a tamyīz; but Abū al-Baqāʾ did not mention its accusative as a tamyīz in the case of making «أَحْصَى» an elative; he mentioned that only when he mentioned that it is a past verb. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "There are two views on «أحصى». First: it is a past verb, «أَمَداً» its object, and «لِما لَبِثوا» an adjective of it, fronted and so becoming a ḥāl, or an object of purpose, i.e. for the sake of their tarrying. It is said: the lām is redundant and «ما» means «الذي», and «أَمَداً» is the object of «لبثوا»; this is a mistake; the right view is rather that it is a tamyīz, the implied form being 'for what they tarried it'. Second: it is a noun, and «أَمَداً» is accusative by a verb indicated by the noun." End of quotation. This is an explicit statement that «أَمَداً», in the case of making «أحصى» a noun, is not a tamyīz but a mafʿūl bihi of an implied verb, and that he made it a tamyīz of «لبثوا», as you have seen.
Then the Shaykh said: "As for his saying: 'or it is accusative by «لبثوا», in which case the meaning is not sound for it', i.e. its meaning would not be sound — al-Ṭabarī held that it is accusative by «لَبِثوا». Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: 'This is not sound.' End of quotation. But it may be sound: that is because al-amad is the limit, and it can express the duration in that the duration is a limit, being in reality the amad of the duration; «ما» means «الذي», and «أمَداً» is accusative by removal of the preposition, its implied form being 'for what they tarried of amad, of duration', so 'of amad' becomes an explanation of what is vague in the word «ما», as in His words {مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ} [al-Baqara: 106] and {مَّا يَفْتَحِ الله لِلنَّاسِ مِن رَّحْمَةٍ} [Fāṭir: 2]; and when the preposition dropped, the verb reached it [directly]."
I say: it suffices him that one like Ibn ʿAṭiyya judged it unsound. And granting that, we do not concede that al-Ṭabarī meant its accusative by «لبثوا» as a mafʿūl bihi; rather, he may have meant its accusative as a tamyīz, as Abū al-Baqāʾ said.
Then he said: "As for his saying 'If you claim …' to the end, we say: that is not needed, because whoever says that may follow the position of the Kufans, that «القوانس» is accusative by «أَضْرَبُ» itself. For that reason some grammarians held that «أعلم» governs «مَنْ» in accusative in His words «أَعْلَمُ مَنْ يَضِلُّ»; that is because the elative includes the meaning of the maṣdar (verbal noun), since the implied form is: our striking the helmet-tops exceeds the striking of others."
I say: this is a less favoured position; the elative is weak, and for that reason it falls short of the adjective resembling the active participle (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha), in that it is not made feminine, dual or plural.
If we make «أَحْصَى» a noun, the Shaykh allowed «أيّ» to be the relative, with «أَحْصَى» the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject) that is its referent, and the ḍamma being that of indeclinability (bināʾ) according to the position of Sībawayh, because/ the condition of indeclinability is present, namely its being annexed in wording and the omission of the head of its ṣila (relative clause). This can only be on making knowing (ʿilm) mean acquaintance (ʿirfān), because there is only one object in the speech, and assuming another is unnecessary. However, ascribing «عَلِمَ» in the sense of «عَرَف» to Allah the Exalted involves a difficulty whose analysis was given in al-Anfāl and elsewhere. If we make it a verb, it is impossible for it [أيّ] to be a relative, since there is then no reason for its indeclinability; and this is good.

semin-durr:13-13.t: The words of Allah the Exalted: {آمَنُواْ بِرَبِّهِمْ}: in it is a shift (iltifāt) from the first person to the third, since had it come in the order of the speech it would have been said: "They were youths who believed in Us." His words «وزِدْناهُم» and «وَرَبَطْنا» are also a shift from this third person back to the first person.

semin-durr:14-14.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {إِذْ قَامُواْ}: accusative by «رَبَطْنا». "Binding" is a metaphor for strengthening their hearts in that slippery situation.
His words: «إذن»: [a particle of] answer and requital, i.e. "we would have said an outrageous saying if we called upon a god besides Him". Shaṭaṭan is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun); one says شَطَّ شَطَطاً وشُطُوطاً, i.e. he was unjust and exceeded his limit; from it: شطَّ في السَّوْمِ and أَشَطَّ, i.e. he exceeded the measure in bargaining. شَطَّ المنزلُ, "the dwelling was far", is from that; and شَطَّتِ الجاريةُ شِطاطاً, "the girl grew tall", is from that. There are three views on its accusative. The position of Sībawayh is that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun of the maṣdar of «قُلْنا». Second: an adjective of a maṣdar, i.e. "a saying possessing outrage", or it is the outrage itself, by hyperbole. Third: that it is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of «قُلْنا», because it includes the meaning of a clause.

semin-durr:15-15.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {هؤلاء قَوْمُنَا اتخذوا}: «قومُنا» may be a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition), with «اتَّخذوا» the khabar (predicate) of «هؤلاء»; or «قومُنا» may be the khabar and «اتَّخذوا» a ḥāl (circumstantial). «اتَّخذ» may take one object, meaning "they made", because they carved them with their hands; or it may take two objects, meaning "they made into", with «مِنْ دونِه» the second, fronted, and «آلهةً» the first. On the first view, «مِنْ دونِه» may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to «اتَّخذوا», or attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl of «آلهة», since if it were placed after it, it could be an adjective of «آلهةً».
His words: {لَّوْلاَ يَأْتُونَ}: an urging (taḥḍīḍ) carrying the meaning of disapproval. «عليهم», i.e. "for their worship" or "for their being taken [as gods]"; the muḍāf was omitted because it is known. This urging clause may not be an adjective of «آلهةً», because it is corrupt in meaning and in grammar, since it is a request clause. If you say: I will imply [a verb of] saying, as in his words:
313 - 0- جاؤُوا بِمَذْقٍ هل رَأَيْتَ الذئبَ قطّْ ...
(They brought diluted milk — [of which one would say:] "Have you ever seen the wolf?")
— the meaning does not assist you, because it is corrupt on that [basis].

semin-durr:16-16.t:
