The words of Allah the Exalted: {وَإِذِ اعتزلتموهم}: «إذا» [Translator's note: so in the text; the word is «إذ»] is accusative by an omitted element, i.e. "and some of them said to others at the time of their withdrawing". Some allowed «إذ» to be causal, i.e. "so take refuge in the cave because of your withdrawing from them"; it is a view that has been stated, but it is not valid.
His words: {وَمَا يَعْبُدُونَ}: three views are possible for «ما». First: that it means «الذي», with the referent pronoun implied, i.e. "and you have withdrawn from what they worship". In «إلا الله», it may be a connected exception (muttaṣil) — for it is narrated that they used to worship Allah and associate others with Him — or disconnected (munqaṭiʿ) — for it is narrated that they worshipped idols only. That from which exception is made may be the relative or its referent pronoun; the meaning is the same.
Second: that it is maṣdariyya, i.e. "and you have withdrawn from their worship", i.e. abandoned it; and «إلا اللهَ» is with omission of a muḍāf, i.e. "except the worship of Allah". The exception has the two preceding views.
Third: that it is negative, and that it is from the speech of Allah the Exalted; on this view this clause is parenthetical within the story; al-Zamakhsharī held this. {إِلاَّ الله} is an emptied exception (istithnāʾ mufarragh): Allah reports of the youths that they worship none other than Him. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: "The third: that it is a particle of negation; then two views come out regarding the exception: first, it is disconnected; second, it is connected; and the meaning is: and when you withdrew from them, except Allah, and they worship none but Allah." I say: the apparent sense of this statement is that disconnection and connection in the exception depend on the view that «ما» is negative, and the matter is not so.
His words: «مِرْفَقا»: the majority read with kasra on the mīm and fatḥa on the fāʾ; Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir the reverse [مَرْفِقاً]. There is disagreement among the lexicographers about the two. It is said: they have one meaning, namely that which one makes use of (yartafiqu bihi), and it is not a maṣdar (verbal noun). It is said: with kasra on the mīm it is for the hand [the elbow], and with fatḥa for affairs, and each may be used in place of the other; al-Azharī reported this from Thaʿlab. Al-Farrāʾ cited, combining the two forms for the limb:
313 - 1- بِتُّ أُجافي مِرْفقاً عن مَرْفقِ ...
(I spent the night keeping one elbow [مِرفق] away from the other elbow [مَرفق].)
/ It is said: both are used together for affairs and for the limb; al-Zajjāj reported this.
Makkī reported that al-Farrāʾ said: "I know only kasra on the mīm, for the affair, for the hand, and for everything."
I say: the mutawātir transmission of the reading of Nāfiʿ and the Syrians refutes him. Al-Kisāʾī rejected kasra on the mīm for the limb and said: "I know only fatḥa in it" — which is the reverse of what his student said. But Abū Ḥātim contradicted him and said: "With fatḥa on the mīm it is the place, like masjid." Abū Zayd said: "With fatḥa on the mīm it is a maṣdar that came on the pattern mafʿal." Some said: they are two dialectal forms for that which one makes use of; as for the limb, it is with kasra on the mīm only. It is reported that al-Farrāʾ said: "The people of the Ḥijāz say «مَرْفقا», with fatḥa on the mīm and kasra on the fāʾ, for what you make use of, and they say mirfaq with kasra for the human [elbow]; and the [other] Arabs afterwards say both with kasra on the mīm." Muʿādh permitted fatḥa on the mīm and the fāʾ [مَرْفَقاً], and it is a maṣdar like al-maḍrab and al-maqtal.
{مِّنْ أَمْرِكُمْ} is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb before it, «مِنْ» being for the beginning of the extent or partitive. It is said: it means "in place of" (badal); Ibn al-Anbārī said this, and he cited:
313 - 2- فليت لنا مِنْ ماءِ زمزمِ شَرْبَةً ... مُبَرَّدَةً باتَتْ على طَهَيانِ
(Would that we had, in place of [مِن] Zamzam water, a draught cooled overnight on Ṭahayān.)
i.e. in place of. It may also be a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «مِرْفَقاً», and so attached to an omitted element.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {تَّزَاوَرُ}: Ibn ʿĀmir read «تَزْوَرُّ» on the measure of taḥmarru; the Kufans «تَزَاوَرُ» with the zāy undoubled; and the rest with it doubled [تَزَّاوَرُ]. «تَزْوَرُّ» means "inclines", from al-zawar, which is inclining; زاره means "he inclined towards him"; qawl al-zūr (false speech) is inclining away from the truth; and from it is al-azwar, one who inclines, with his eye or otherwise. ʿUmar ibn Abī Rabīʿa said:
313 - 3-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . وجَنْبي خِيفة القوم أَزْوَرُ
(… while my side, for fear of the people, is turned away [أزور].)
It is said: تَزْوَرُّ means "contracts", from ازْوَرَّ, i.e. contracted; and from it is the verse of ʿAntara:
313 - 4- فازْوَرَّ مَنْ وَقَعَ القَنا بلَبانِه ... وشكا إليَّ بعَبْرَةٍ وتَحَمْحُمِ
(He [the horse] shrank away [ازورّ] from the fall of the spears on his breast, and complained to me with a tear and a whinny.)
It is said: [it means] inclined. Similar is the verse of Bishr ibn Abī Khāzim:
313 - 5- يَؤُمُ بها الحداةُ مياهَ نَخْلٍ ... وفيها عن أبانَيْنِ ازْوِرارُ
(The camel-drivers head with them for the waters of Nakhl, while in them there is a veering [ازورار] away from the two Abāns.)
i.e. an inclining.
As for «تزاوَرُ» and «تَّوازَرُ» [Translator's note: so in the text; the second form intended is «تَزَّاوَرُ», the doubled reading], their origin is tatazāwaru with two tāʾs; the Kufans dropped one of the two tāʾs and the others assimilated; the precise treatment of this was given at «تَظَاهَرون», «تَساءلون» and the like. Its meaning is also inclining.
Abū Rajāʾ, al-Jaḥdarī, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Ayyūb al-Sakhtiyānī read «تَزْوَارُّ» on the measure of taḥmārru. ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] and Abū al-Mutawakkil read «تَزْوَئِرُّ» with a hamza with kasra before a doubled rāʾ; its origin is «تَزْوارُّ», as in the reading of Abū Rajāʾ and those with him, but he disliked the combination of two quiescents and changed the alif into a hamza, in the manner of its change in «جَأَنّ» and «الضَّأَلِّين». The precise treatment of this was given at the beginning of this work, at the end of al-Fātiḥa.
{إِذَا طَلَعَت} is governed by «تَرَى» or by «تَزَاوَرُ»; likewise {إِذَا غَرَبَت} is governed by the first or by the second, namely «تَقْرضهم». The apparent view is that it is purely adverbial; it may also be conditional.
The meaning of «تَقْرِضُهم» is "it cuts them off, not coming near them", because al-qarḍ is cutting, from severance and cutting off. Dhū al-Rumma said:
313 - 6- إلى ظُعُنٍ يَقْرِضْنَ أقْواز مُشْرِفٍ ... شِمالاً، وعن أَيْمَانِهِنَّ الفوارِسُ
(Towards litters of women that cut past [يقرضن] the sand-hills of Mushrif on the left, with al-Fawāris on their right.)
Al-qarḍ is cutting; its precise treatment was given in al-Baqara. Al-Fārisī said: "The meaning of تَقْرِضُهم is: it gives them something of its light and then quickly departs, like a loan (qarḍ) that is taken back." His view was judged weak on the ground that it should then be read «تُقْرِضُهم» with ḍamma on the tāʾ, since it would be from أَقْرض.
It was also read «يَقْرِضهم» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, i.e. the cave; this involves a discrepancy between the two verbs and their agents, so it is better that it refer to the sun, and be like his words:
313 - 7-. . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولا أرضَ أَبْقَلَ إبْقالَها
(… nor any land that has brought forth herbage [أبقل, masculine] like its bringing forth.)
This is the view of Ibn Kaysān.
«ذات اليمين» and «ذات الشِّمال» are two adverbs of place (ẓarf makān) meaning "the direction of the right" and "the direction of the left".
His words: {وَهُمْ فِي فَجْوَةٍ مِّنْهُ}: a circumstantial clause (ḥāliyya), i.e. "We do this despite the spaciousness of their place", which is more wondrous for their situation, since the sun should have reached them because of its spaciousness. Al-fajwa is the spacious place, from al-fajā, which is a wide gap between the thighs; one says "a man afjā" and "a woman fajwāʾ". The plural of fajwa is fijāʾ, like qaṣʿa and qiṣāʿ.
His words: «ذلك»: a mubtadaʾ (subject) referring to everything that preceded of their story, and «من آياتِ الله» is the khabar (predicate). «ذلك» may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "the matter is that", with {مِنْ آيَاتِ الله} a ḥāl (circumstantial).

semin-durr:18-18.t:
The words of Allah the Exalted: {أَيْقَاظاً}: the plural of «يَقُظ» with ḍamma on the qāf; it is also pluralised as yiqāẓ. Yaquẓ and ayqāẓ are like ʿaḍud and aʿḍād; yaquẓ and yiqāẓ like rajul and rijāl. The apparent sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words is that one says «يَقِظ» with kasra, for he said: "Ayqāẓ is the plural of «يَقِظ», like ankād of «نَكِد»." Al-yaqaẓa is wakefulness, the opposite of sleep.
Al-ruqūd is the plural of rāqid (sleeping), like qāʿid and quʿūd. There is no need to imply anything, as some said, that the implied form is: "had you seen them, you would have thought them awake."
His words: «ونُقَلِّبهم»: the majority read «نُقَلِّبهم», an imperfect predicated of the One who magnifies Himself. It was also read likewise with the lower-dotted yāʾ, i.e. Allah or the angel. Al-Ḥasan read «يُقْلِبُهم» with the lower-dotted yāʾ, sukūn on the qāf and the lām undoubled, its fāʿil (agent) being as before: either Allah or the angel. He also read «وتَقَلُّبَهم», with fatḥa on the tāʾ and ḍamma on the doubled lām, the maṣdar (verbal noun) of تَقَلَّبَ — as in His words {وَتَقَلُّبَكَ فِي الساجدين} [al-Shuʿarāʾ: 219] — with the bāʾ accusative. Abū al-Fatḥ [Ibn Jinnī] explained it by an implied verb, i.e. "and We see their turning", or "We witness". It is also narrated from him with the bāʾ nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject), the khabar (predicate) being the adverbial phrase after it; or it may be omitted, i.e. "[is] a great sign"./ ʿIkrima read «وتَقْلِبُهم» with the feminine tāʾ, the imperfect of «قَلَب» undoubled, its fāʿil being the pronoun of the angels indicated by the context.
His words: «وكَلْبُهم»: the majority read thus. Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq read «كالِبُهم», i.e. the owner of their dog, like lābin (owner of milk) and tāmir (owner of dates). Abū ʿUmar al-Zāhid, Ghulām Thaʿlab, transmitted «وكالِئُهم», with a hamza with ḍamma, an active participle of كَلأَ يكلأُ, i.e. to guard.
«باسِط» is an active participle with past [meaning]; it governs only by way of relating a past state as present (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl). Al-Kisāʾī makes it govern [in the past] and cites this verse as evidence.
Al-waṣīd is the door. It is said: the threshold; it is said: the ground and earth; it is said: the courtyard. [The poet] cited:
313 - 8- بأرضِ فضاءٍ لا يُسَدُّ وَصِيْدُها ... عليَّ ومعروفي بها غيرُ مُنكَرِ
(In an open land whose entrance [وصيد] is not closed to me, and my kindness there is not unacknowledged.)
The majority read the wāw of {لَوِ اطلعت} with kasra, according to the basic rule of the meeting of two quiescents. Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba, Nāfiʿ, Ibn Waththāb and al-Aʿmash read it with ḍamma, by analogy with the wāw of the pronoun; its precise treatment was given earlier.
His words: «فِرارا»: it may be accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun) from the meaning of the verb before it, because turning away and fleeing are of one kind. It may be a maṣdar in the position of a ḥāl (circumstantial), i.e. "fleeing", being an emphatic ḥāl. And it may be an object of purpose (mafʿūl lahu).
His words: «رُعْباً»: a second object; it is said: a tamyīz (specification). Ibn Kathīr and Nāfiʿ read «لَمُلِّئْتَ» with doubling, for intensiveness; Abū Jaʿfar and Shayba likewise, except with the hamza changed into a yāʾ. Al-Zuhrī read with the lām undoubled and with the change [into yāʾ], which is a regular change. The disagreement over «الرعب» was given in Āl ʿImrān.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His words: {وكذلك بَعَثْنَاهُمْ}: the kāf is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "just as We made them sleep that sleep, so We raised them", as a reminder of His power. The reference by «ذلك» is to the maṣdar understood from His words «فَضَرَبْنا», i.e. "like Our making their sleep for this long period a sign, We made their raising a sign"; al-Zajjāj and al-Zamakhsharī said this.
His words: «ليتساءَلُوا»: the lām is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the raising. It is said: it is [the lām] of outcome (ṣayrūra), because the raising was not for the purpose of asking one another; Ibn ʿAṭiyya said this. The correct view is that it has its basic causal meaning.
His words: {كَم لَبِثْتُمْ}: «كم» is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), and the specifying noun (tamyīz) is omitted, its implied form being "how many days", because the answer indicates it. «أَوْ» in His words «أو بعضَ يوم» is for doubt on their part; it is said: for detailing, i.e. some of them said this and some that.
His words: «بِوَرِقِكم»: a ḥāl (circumstantial) of «أحدَكم», i.e. accompanying it and invested with it. Abū ʿAmr, Ḥamza and Abū Bakr read with fatḥa on the wāw, sukūn on the rāʾ, and without assimilation [بِوَرْقِكم]; the rest of the Seven with kasra on the rāʾ. The kasra is the original, and the sukūn is a lightening, like «نَبْق» for nabiq. Al-Zajjāj reported kasra on the wāw with sukūn on the rāʾ [بِوِرْقِكم], which is a transfer [of the vowel], just as one says kabid, kabd and kibd.
Abū Rajāʾ and Ibn Muḥayṣin read likewise, except with assimilation of the qāf [into the kāf]. They considered it weak in that it combines two quiescents not in their proper conditions; but you have had in the mutawātir [readings] what resembles this, such as {فَنِعِمَّا} and {لاَ تَعْدُّواْ فِي السبت} [al-Nisāʾ: 154] … It is narrated from Ibn Muḥayṣin that he assimilated, giving the rāʾ kasra [Translator's note: the text reads «أَدْغَمَ كسرَ الراءَ»], to escape what you mentioned.
The Commander of the Believers [ʿAlī] read «بوارِقِكم», an active participle, i.e. possessor of silver, like «لابِن». It is said: it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), like jāmil (a herd of camels) and bāqir (a herd of cattle).
Al-wariq is minted silver; it is said: silver in general. It is also called «الرِّقَةُ», with the first radical dropped; in the ḥadīth: «في الرِّقَةِ رُبْع العُشْر» ("On silver [is due] a quarter of a tenth"). It was anomalously given the sound masculine plural; they said: «حُبُّ الرِّقَيْنِ يغطِّي أَفْن الأَفِين» ("Love of silver coins covers the foolishness of the fool").
His words: «أيُّها أَزْكَى»: «أيّ» may be interrogative, or relative; you have learnt that from what was given earlier at His words {أَيُّهُم أَحْسَنُ عَمَلاً} [al-Kahf: 7], for the analysis is the same. An omission is necessary: "which of its people is purer". «طعاماً» is a tamyīz (specification). It is said: there is no omission, and the pronoun refers to the foods indicated by the context.
His words: «ولِيَتَلَطَّفْ»: the majority read with sukūn on the lām of the imperative, and al-Ḥasan with kasra on it, according to the original. Qutayba al-Mayyāl read «ولِيُتَلَطَّفْ» in the passive. Abū Jaʿfar, Abū Ṣāliḥ and Qutayba read «ولا يَشْعُرَن» with fatḥa on the yāʾ and ḍamma on the ʿayn, «أحدٌ» being its fāʿil (agent).
[Translator's note: the source writes Qutayba's passive reading with the same vowelling as the majority, «ولِيَتَلَطَّفْ»; it is rendered here as «ولِيُتَلَطَّفْ» per the stated passive.]

semin-durr:20-20.t: His saying: {إِنَّهُمْ}. This pronoun may refer back to «أحد» because it is plural in meaning, and it may refer to «أهل» (the people) that is annexed to the pronoun of the city; al-Zamakhsharī said this. It may also refer to «قومِهم» (their people), since the context indicates them. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read «يُظْهِروا» in the passive. And «إذن» is a response and a consequence, that is: if they gain the upper hand, you will not prosper.

semin-durr:21-21.t:
His saying: {وكذلك أَعْثَرْنَا}: that is, just as We made them sleep and raised them up, so We made [people] stumble upon them (aʿtharnā), that is, We made them aware. The discussion of the root «عثر» has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Māʾida. And «لِيَعْلَموا» is attached to «أَعْثَرْنا». As for the pronoun, it was said that it refers to the omitted direct object (mafʿūl bihi) of «أَعْثَرْنا», its implied form being "We made the people stumble upon them"; and it was said that it refers to the People of the Cave.

His saying: {إِذْ يَتَنَازَعُونَ}. It is permissible that «أَعْثَرنا» governs it, or «لِيَعْلَموا», or the sense of «حَقٌّ», or «وَعْدَ», according to those who allow latitude with the adverbial (ẓarf). As for those who do not allow latitude, it is not permissible to make a predication about the relative noun before its ṣila (relative clause) is complete.

His saying: «بُنْياناً». It may be a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), the plural of «يُنْيَانَه» [sic], and it may be a maṣdar (verbal noun).

His saying: {رَّبُّهُمْ أَعْلَمُ بِهِمْ}. It may be the speech of the Creator, the Exalted, and it may be the speech of the two parties disputing about them.

His saying: «غَلَبوا». ʿĪsā al-Thaqafī and al-Ḥasan read it with ḍamma on the ghayn and kasra on the lām.

[Translator's note: the source prints «يُنْيَانَه» as the singular of «بُنْياناً»; the word appears to be garbled in the text (presumably «بُنْيَانَة») and is reproduced as written.]

semin-durr:22-22.t:
His saying: {سَيَقُولُونَ}: It was said that the sīn was brought here only because the discourse contains an ellipsis and an implicit inclusion (ṭayy and idmāj), its implied form being: when you have answered them about their question concerning the story of the People of the Cave, then ask them about their number, for they will say… And it was not brought with the remaining verbs because they are conjoined to the one that has the sīn, so they were given its rule of futurity.

Ibn Muḥayṣin read «ثَلاثٌّ» with assimilation (idghām) of the thā' (the three-dotted letter) into the tā' of the feminine, because their points of articulation are close, because both are voiceless, and because they come after a quiescent weak letter.

His saying: {رَّابِعُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ}: The clause is in the position of nominative as a ṣifa (adjective) of «ثلاثة».

His saying: «خَمْسَةٌ». Ibn Kathīr, in one transmission, read it with fatḥa on the mīm, which is a dialectal form like «عَشَرَة». Ibn Muḥayṣin read it with kasra on the khā' and the mīm, and with assimilation of the tā' into the sīn, meaning the tā' of «خمسة» into the sīn of «سادسهم». This is an extremely heavy reading, with two consecutive kasras and three sīns, and I think nothing like this can be anything but a mistake attributed to such a man. It is also transmitted from him that he assimilated the tanwīn into the sīn without nasalisation (ghunna).

«ثلاثةٌ», «خمسةٌ» and «سبعةٌ» are predicates of an implied subject, that is: they are three, they are five, they are seven. The clause after «ثلاثة» and «خمسة» is an adjective of both, as already mentioned. It is not permissible for the clause to be a ḥāl (circumstantial), because there is no governor in it; nor is it permissible for the implied form to be "These are three, these are five," with the governor being the demonstrative or the particle of attention. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Because that is a pointing to something present, and they did not point to something present."

His saying: {رَجْماً بالغيب}. There are four possibilities in it. The first: that it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); they say that for the sake of casting at the unseen. The second: that it is in the position of ḥāl, that is, conjecturing. The third: that it is accusative by «يقولون», because it is close to it in meaning. The fourth: that it is accusative by an implied verb of the same root, that is: they cast [conjecture] with that a casting.

Rajm originally means throwing with rijām, which are small stones; then it was used figuratively for conjecture. Zuhayr said:

313-9- وما الحربُ إلا ما عَلِمْتُمْ وذُقْتُمُ ... وما هو عنها بالحديثِ المُرَجَّمِ
(War is nothing but what you have known and tasted; it is not, about it, a conjectured report.)

that is, one that is merely conjectured.

His saying: «وثامِنُهُم». There are several possibilities concerning this wāw. The first: that it is a conjunction, conjoining this clause to the clause «هم سبعة», so that they would have given two predications: one, that they are seven men, categorically; and the other, that their eighth is their dog. This implies that the clause {وَثَامِنُهُمْ كَلْبُهُمْ} is the speech of those disputing about them. The second: that the wāw is resumptive, and that it is the speech of Allah the Exalted, informing about them thus. This speaker said: the wāw was brought to give the sense of separation from what precedes. The third: that it is the wāw that enters upon the adjective for emphasis and to indicate the attachment of the adjective to the thing described. Al-Zamakhsharī took this view, and compared it with His saying: {مِن قَرْيَةٍ إِلاَّ وَلَهَا كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ} [al-Ḥijr: 4]. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected it, saying that none of the grammarians had said it; the discussion of this has already been given.

The fourth: that this is called the "wāw of eight," and that in the dialect of Quraysh, when they count, they say: five, six, seven and eight, nine — so they insert the wāw specifically at the knot of eight. Ibn Khālawayh and Abū Bakr, the transmitter of ʿĀṣim, mentioned this. I say: some have said this about His saying, the Exalted: {وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوَابُهَا} [verse 73] in [Sūrat] al-Zumar, saying: it was inserted in the case of the gates of Paradise because they are eight, and for that reason it was not brought in the case of the gates of Hell because they are seven. This will come, if Allah wills.

It was also read: «كالبُهم», that is, "the owner of their dog." Because of this reading some posited, for the reading of the majority: "and their eighth is the owner of their dog."

«ثلاثة», «خمسة» and «سبعة» are annexed to an omitted counted noun. The Shaykh posited it as "three persons," saying: "We posited 'persons' only because «رابعهم» is an active participle annexed to the pronoun, and the meaning is that he made them four (rabaʿahum), that is, he made them four and brought them to this number. Had we posited 'men,' it would be impossible for him to turn three men into four because of the difference of the two kinds." This is a fine statement.

Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "The active participle does not govern here because it is past." I say: he means that «رابعهم» refers to what is past, so it does not govern accusative even by implication, and the annexation is a true (maḥḍa) one. It is not as he claimed, for the meaning is "the dog becomes for them the fourth," so it governs accusative by implication, and it governs although it is past because of the narration of a present state (ḥikāyat al-ḥāl), like «باسط».

[Translator's note: the source reads «وعي قراءة» where «وهي قراءة» is evidently meant ("and it is a reading"), and «لم يُجَأْ بها» for «لم يُجَأْ/يُجَىْء بها»; both are translated by sense. The poetry number "313 - 9-" is as printed.]

semin-durr:24-24.t:
His saying, the Exalted: {إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ الله}. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "There are three possibilities regarding the excepted-from (mustathnā minhu). The first: it is from the prohibition, and the meaning is: do not say, 'I will do it tomorrow,' unless you are permitted to say it. The second: it is from «فاعلٌ» (doer), that is: do not say 'I will do it tomorrow' until you join with it the saying 'if Allah wills.' The third: that it is a discontinuous exception (munqaṭiʿ). The position of «أَنْ يشاء اللهُ» is accusative in two ways. One is as an exception, the implied form being: do not say that at any time except the time when Allah wills, that is, permits; so the time is omitted though it is intended. The other is that it is a ḥāl, the implied form being: do not say 'I will do it tomorrow' except saying 'if Allah wills'; and omission of the saying is frequent. He made His saying «إلا أن يشاء» of the sense of «إن شاء», which is among what is construed according to the meaning. And it was said that the implied form is 'except with Allah's willing,' that is, accompanied by the saying 'if Allah wills.'"

I say: al-Zamakhsharī rejected the second possibility, saying: "«إلا أَنْ يشاء» is attached to the prohibition, not to His saying «إنِّي فاعلٌ», because had he said 'I will do such and such unless Allah wills,' its meaning would be: unless the will of Allah intervenes to prevent his doing it, and that is something in which the prohibition has no place." I say: he means that a prohibition of such a meaning is not fitting.

Then he said: "Its attachment to the prohibition is in two ways. One: do not say that saying unless Allah wills that you say it, by permitting you to do so. The second: do not say it except with Allah's willing, that is, with His will; and this is in the position of ḥāl, that is, accompanied by the will of Allah, saying 'if Allah wills.' There is also a third possibility: that «إلا أن يشاء» has the sense of a word of perpetuity, as if it were said, 'and do not say it ever,' like His saying: {وَمَا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّعُودَ فِيهَآ إِلاَّ أَن يَشَآءَ الله رَبُّنَا} [al-Aʿrāf: 89], because their returning to their religion is something Allah does not will."

What al-Zamakhsharī mentioned was rejected by Ibn ʿAṭiyya, after relating it from al-Ṭabarī and others, without making clear the point of its invalidity.

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "«وإلا أَنْ يشاءَ اللهُ» is an exception that cannot be taken at face value, because it would then fall under the saying and be part of what is said; and Allah does not forbid him to say 'I will do that tomorrow unless Allah wills,' because it is a statement sound in itself and it is not possible to forbid it. So an implied element was needed to interpret this apparent sense. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: 'There is an omission in the discourse that the apparent sense requires and that brevity makes fine, its implied form being: except that you say, "except that Allah wills," or except that you say, "if Allah wills." The meaning is: except that you mention the will of Allah; so «إلا أن يشاءَ اللهُ» is not part of the saying that was forbidden.'"

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {ثَلاثَ مِئَةٍ سِنِينَ}. The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read it with annexation of «مِئَةِ» to «سنين»; the rest read «مِئَةٍ» with tanwīn. As for the first reading, they placed the plural in the position of the singular, as in His saying: {بالأخسرين أَعْمَالاً} [al-Kahf: 103]. Al-Zamakhsharī said this, meaning that he placed «أَعْمالاً» in the position of «عَمَلاً». Abū Ḥātim attacked this reading, but he is not to be heeded. In the codex of ʿAbd Allāh it is «سَنَة», in the singular, and Ubayy read it so. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «سِنُون» with wāw, as the predicate of an implied subject, that is: they are years.

As for the rest: since they did not see annexation of «مِئَة» to a plural, they put tanwīn and made «سِنين» a badal (substitute) for «ثلثمئة», or an ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition). Abū l-Baqāʾ reported that it is a badal from «مِئَة» because it has the sense of a plural. It is not permissible for «سنين» in this reading to be a tamyīz (specification), because that comes only by necessity, with a singular specifier, as in his saying:

314-0- إذا عاش الفَتَى مِئَتين عاماً ... [فقد] ذَهَب اللَّذاذَةُ والفَتاءُ
(When a young man has lived two hundred years, then pleasure and youth have gone.)

His saying: «تِسْعاً», that is, nine years; the specified noun (mumayyaz) was omitted because what precedes indicates it, since one does not say "I have three hundred dirhams and nine" except meaning nine dirhams; and had you meant garments or the like it would not be permitted, because it would be an enigma. «تِسْعاً» is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object). And «ازداد» is of the form ifta'ala, the tā' having been changed to dāl after the zāy; it was transitive to two objects, as in {وَزِدْنَاهُمْ هُدًى} [al-Kahf: 13], but when it was built on the ifta'ala pattern it lost one.

Al-Ḥasan, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, read «تَسْعا» with fatḥa on the tā', like «عَشْر».

[Translator's note: the source reads «وراية» for «رواية» ("transmission"); translated by sense.]

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {أَبْصِرْ بِهِ}. It is a form of wonder (taʿajjub) meaning "how clear-sighted He is" (mā abṣarahu), figuratively; and the hā' refers to Allah the Exalted. In a case like this there are three views. The soundest is that it is in the form of an imperative and its meaning is a statement, and the bā' is redundant in the agent, to make the wording sound. The second: that the agent is a pronoun of the maṣdar. The third: that it is the pronoun of the one addressed, that is: "cause [to see], O one addressed." It was also said: it is truly an imperative, not an expression of wonder, and the hā' refers to the guidance (al-hudā) understood from the discourse.

ʿĪsā read «أَسْمَعَ» and «أَبْصَرَ» as past verbs, the agent being Allah the Exalted, and likewise the hā' in «به», that is: He saw His servants and made them hear.

His saying: «مِنْ وليّ». It may be an agent, and it may be a mubtadaʾ (subject).

His saying: «ولا يُشْرك». Ibn ʿĀmir read it with tā' and the jussive, that is: "and do not associate [anyone], you, O human." The rest read it with yā' (the two dots below) and the verb in the nominative, that is: and Allah does not associate anyone in His judgment; so it is a pure negation.

Mujāhid read «ولا يُشْرِكْ» with the tā' from below (بالتاء من تحتُ) and the jussive. [Translator's note: this is the wording of the source; "tā' from below" is probably a slip for the yā' (two dots below).]

Yaʿqūb said: "I do not know its explanation." I say: its explanation is that the agent is the pronoun of the human being, left implied because it is known.

The pronoun in His saying «مالهم» refers to the contemporaries of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "And the verse would be a parenthetical threat (iʿtirāḍ)." It seems he means by "parenthetical" that they are not among those for whose sake the discourse was set out, and he does not mean the technical parenthesis.

semin-durr:28-28.t:
His saying: {واصبر نَفْسَكَ}: that is, restrain it and make it steadfast. Abū Dhuʾayb said:

314-1- فصبَرْتُ عارفةً لذلك حُرَّة ... تَرْسُو إذا نَفْسُ الجبانِ تَطَلَّعُ
(So I held firm — a noble soul that knew this — that stays steady when the soul of the coward cranes upward.)

As for his saying «بالغَداة», the discussion of it has already been given in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām.

His saying: {وَلاَ تَعْدُ عَيْنَاكَ}. There are two possibilities. One: that its object is omitted, the implied form being "and let your eyes not pass beyond the looking." The second: that it is made to carry the sense of what is transitive with «عَنْ». Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It was made transitive with «عَنْ» because «عَدا» was made to carry the sense of «نبا» and «علا», as in your saying 'his eye slipped away from him' and 'his eye rose above him,' when it passes over him and does not settle on him. If you say: what is the purpose of this implication (tadmīn)? Why was it not said 'and let not your eyes pass beyond them,' or 'let not your eyes rise above them'? I say: the purpose is to give the sum of two meanings, and that is stronger than giving a single meaning. Do you not see how the meaning comes back to your saying: 'and do not let your eyes plunge past them, going beyond them to others'? Similar is {وَلاَ تأكلوا أَمْوَالَهُمْ إلى أَمْوَالِكُمْ} [al-Nisāʾ: 2], that is, 'do not add them to yours, consuming them.'"

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] rejected him, since the position of the Basrans is that tadmīn is not subject to analogy and is resorted to only in necessity; when it is possible to avoid it, it is not resorted to.

Al-Ḥasan read «ولا تُعْدِ عَيْنَيْكَ» from the quadriliteral-form aʿdā. He, ʿĪsā and al-Aʿmash read «ولا تُعَدِّ» with shadda, from ʿaddā yuʿaddī in the intensive form; he made it transitive in the first with the hamza and in the second by doubling, as in the saying of al-Nābigha:

314-2- فَعَدَّ عَمَّا تَرَى إذ لا ارْتِجاعَ له ... وانْمِ القُتُوْدَ على عَيْرانَةٍ أُجُدِ
(So pass beyond what you see, since it cannot be recovered, and raise the saddles upon a sturdy, swift she-camel.)

Thus said al-Zamakhsharī and Abū l-Faḍl. The Shaykh objected to both of them: if its transitivity in these two readings were by the hamza or the doubling, it would be transitive to two objects, since before that it is transitive to one by itself. Al-Zamakhsharī admitted that where he said: "It is said ʿadāhu when he passes beyond it, and it was made transitive with ʿan only because it implies the meaning of ʿalā and nabā; so in that case the forms afʿala and faʿʿala agree with the bare stem." It is a fine objection.

His saying: «تُريد» is a circumstantial clause (ḥāl). It is permissible that the agent of «تريد» be the one addressed, that is: you desire; and it is permissible that it be the pronoun of the two eyes, and it is in the singular only because the two are inseparable, so a predicate of a single thing may be predicated of both. From this is the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

314-3- لِمَنْ زُحْلُوقَةٌ زُلَّ ... بها العَيْنان تَنْهَلُّ
(Whose is the slide, from which, upon it, the two eyes pour forth tears?)

and the saying of another:

314-4- وكأنَّ في العينين حَبَّ قَرَنْفُلٍ ... أو سُنْبُلاً كُحِلَتْ به فانهَلَّتِ
(As if in the two eyes were clove-seeds or spikenard with which they were kohl-ed, and they poured forth.)

There is more besides that. Ascribing desire to the two eyes is figurative. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "The clause is in the position of ḥāl." The Shaykh said: "As for the owner of the ḥāl, if «عيناك» is assumed, the construction would have been «تريدان»." I say: he overlooked the rule I have mentioned, that two inseparable things may be predicated of as one. Then he said: "And if the kāf is assumed, then having a ḥāl come from a genitive by annexation like this is problematic, because of the difference between the governor of the ḥāl and the owner of the ḥāl.

Some have permitted that when the annexed noun is a part, or like a part, and what makes it good is that the one intended by the prohibition is he, upon him be peace. «عيناك» was brought although he is the one intended, because by the two eyes regard for the person and turning toward him is made."

I say: a fine possibility has appeared to me that I have seen no one but me mention: that «تَعْدُ» is predicated of the pronoun of the one addressed ﷺ, and «عيناك» is a badal (substitute) from the pronoun, a partial substitute for the whole. And «تُرِيدُ» is in both its aspects: as a ḥāl from «عيناك» or from the pronoun in «تَعْدُ». However, in making it a ḥāl from the pronoun in «ولا تَعْدُ» there is weakness, in that regard for the word substituted for, after mention of the substitute, is very rare. You say: "The girl, her beauty is bewitching (fātin, masculine)," and «فاتنة» (feminine) is not permitted except rarely, as in his saying:

314-5- فكأنَّه لِهقُ السَّراةِ كأنَّه ... ما حاجِبَيْهِ مُعَيَّنٌ بسَوادِ
(As if he were a white-backed one, as if — what of his two eyebrows — [one] marked out with black.)

He said «مُعَيَّنٌ» (singular) out of regard for the hā' in «كأنه», whereas the eloquent form would be «مُعَيَّنان» out of regard for «حاجبيه», which is the substitute.

His saying: {أَغْفَلْنَا قَلْبَهُ}. The majority attribute the verb to «نا», with «قلبَه» a direct object. ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd ibn Fāʾid and Mūsā al-Aswārī read it with fatḥa on the lām and the nominative «قلبُه», attributing the heedlessness to the heart. There are several explanations in it. Ibn Jinnī said: "Him whom we regarded as heedless of it." Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Him whose heart we reckoned heedless, from 'I found him heedless' (aghfaltuhu)." Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "There are two ways: one, 'we found his heart turning away from it'; the second: 'he neglected our command out of remembering us.'"

His saying: «فُرُطاً». It may be an adjective on the pattern fuʿul, as in their saying "a farasun furuṭ," that is, one that is ahead of the horses; likewise here, that is, "ahead of the truth." It may be a maṣdar in the sense of tafrīṭ (neglect) or ifrāṭ (excess). Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Al-furuṭ may have the sense of neglect and wasting, that is, his affair that he ought to hold to; and it may have the sense of excess and extravagance."

[Translator's note: the quotation marks in this entry follow the source, in which the opening and closing marks are partly garbled; the quotation of Abū Ḥayyān that begins "And if the kāf is assumed" runs through "the person and turning toward him is made" as best as the text allows. The first line of poetry in 314-5 and the source line of 314-3 are given in the sense of the printed text.]

semin-durr:29-29.t:
His saying: {وَقُلِ الحق}. Three possibilities are allowed in it. The first: that it is the khabar (predicate) of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is: this, meaning the Qur'an, or what you have heard, is the truth. The second: that it is the agent of an implied verb that the context indicates, that is: the truth has come, as He made explicit in another place; except that a verb is not implied save in places already pointed out, among them: that it be the response to a question, or be used to reject a negation, or that a passive verb occur whose attribution to what follows is not suitable, as in the reading {يُسَبِّحُ لَهُ فِيهَا بالغدو}, the verification of which will come, if Allah wills, in its place. The third: that it is a mubtadaʾ and its predicate is the prepositional phrase after it.

Abū l-Sammāl Qaʿnab read «وقُلُ الحقَّ» with ḍamma on the lām wherever it occurs, as if as an assimilation to the vowel of the qāf. He also read it with the accusative «الحقَّ». The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ» said: "It is as a description of the implied maṣdar; for the verb indicates its maṣdar even if it is not mentioned, so you make it accusative when definite as you make it accusative when indefinite; its implied form is: and say the true saying; and «مِنْ» is attached to an implied [word] on that basis, that is: it has come from your Lord." End.

Al-Ḥasan and al-Thaqafī read the two lām's of the imperative with kasra in His saying «فَلْيُؤْمِنْ» and «فَلْيَكْفُرْ», which is the original form.

His saying: {فَمَن شَآءَ فَلْيُؤْمِن}. «مَنْ» may be conditional, which is the apparent sense, and may be relative, with the fā' because of its resemblance to a condition. The agent of «شاء» is apparently a pronoun referring to «مَنْ». It was also said: a pronoun referring to Allah, and Ibn ʿAbbās interpreted it so; the majority hold the contrary.

His saying: {أَحَاطَ بِهِمْ سُرَادِقُهَا}: it is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «ناراً». Al-surādiq: it was said that it is whatever encloses something, like a pavilion or tent. It was said that the wall that encloses something is called a surādiq; al-Harawī said this. It was said: it is the chamber that is around the tent. It was said: it is what is stretched over the courtyard of a house. It was said: every house made of cotton is a surādiq. Ruʾba said:

314-6- يا حَكَمُ بنَ المنذرِ بن الجارُوْدْ ... سُرادِقُ المجدِ عليك مَمْدودْ
(O Ḥakam ibn al-Mundhir ibn al-Jārūd, the pavilion of glory is stretched over you.)

One says "a musaradaq house." The poet said:

314-7- هو المُدْخِلُ النُّعْمانَ بيتاً سماؤُه ... صدورُ الفُيولِ بعد بيتٍ مُسَرْدَقِ
(He is the one who put al-Nuʿmān into a house whose sky was the chests of elephants, after a pavilioned house.)

Abarwīz, the king of the Persians, had killed al-Nuʿmān ibn al-Mundhir under the feet of elephants. Al-fuyūl is the plural of fīl. It was also said: al-surādiq is the vestibule. Al-Farazdaq said:

314-8- تَمَنَّيْتَهم حتى إذا ما لَقِيْتَهُمْ ... تركْتَ لهم قبلَ الضِّراب السُّرادقا
(You longed for them, until when you met them you left them, before the fighting, the pavilion.)

Al-surādiq is an Arabised Persian word, originally sarāda; al-Jawālīqī said so. Al-Rāghib said: "It is an Arabised Persian word, and there is no singular noun in their speech whose third letter is an alif followed by two letters."

His saying: {وَإِن يَسْتَغِيثُواْ}, that is, they ask for help. The yā' is from a wāw, since the origin is yastaghwithū, and the wāw was changed to yā' for a morphological reason mentioned in al-Fātiḥa at His saying {نَسْتَعِينُ} [al-Fātiḥa: 5]. This speech is of the nature of correspondence and likeness (mushākala wa-tajānus); otherwise, what relief is there for them in it? Or it is of the category of mockery (tahakkum), as in his saying:

314-9- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... . . . . . . . . فَأُعْتِبُوا بالصَّيْلَمِ
(... and so they were "appeased" with the calamity.)

and as in his saying:

315-0- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... تَحِيَّةُ بينِهم ضَرْبٌ وَجيعُ
(... their greeting among them is a painful blow.)

and it is frequent.

«كالمُهْلِ» is an adjective of «ماء». Al-muhl: the dregs of oil; it was said: what is melted of the metals such as copper and lead. Al-mahal with two fatḥas: gentleness and dignity. He said: {فَمَهِّلِ الكافرين} [al-Ṭāriq: 17].

His saying: {يَشْوِي الوجوه}. The clause may be a second adjective, or a ḥāl from «ماء» because it has been specified by the adjective, and it may be a ḥāl from the genitive, which is the kāf. Al-shayy is cooking by fire without any broth accompanying the thing grilled.

His saying: {بِئْسَ الشراب}. The specified (al-makhṣūṣ) is omitted, its implied form being "it," that is, that water for which help is sought.

His saying: {وَسَآءَتْ مُرْتَفَقاً}. «ساءت» here is conjugated in its normal sense. Its agent is the pronoun of the fire. «مُرْتَفَقَا» is a tamyīz transferred from the agent, that is: its resting-place is bad and ugly. Al-murtafaq: the place of reclining; it was said, the abode; it was said, it is a maṣdar meaning irtifāq (reclining). This is also of the category of correspondence, as in His saying in describing Paradise afterward: {وَحَسُنَتْ مُرْتَفَقاً} [al-Kahf: 31]; otherwise, what reclining is there in the Fire? Al-Zamakhsharī said: unless it is from his saying:

315-1- إني أَرِقْتُ فَبِتُّ الليلَ مُرْتَفِقا ... كأنَّ عَيْنِيَ فيها الصابُ مَذْبوحُ
(I was sleepless and passed the night leaning on my elbow, as if my eye had bitter aloe poured into it.)

meaning, of the category of mockery.

[Translator's note: the opening quotation mark before «أنه فاعلٌ» and several others in this entry are misplaced in the source; they have been rendered by sense. In the source, the poetry numbers 314-9 and 315-0 each begin with lines of dots, indicating omitted hemistichs.]

semin-durr:30-30.t:
His saying: {إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ}: It may be the predicate of {إِنَّ الذين}. The link (rābiṭ) is either the repetition of the overt noun in its meaning, which is the view of al-Akhfash — and the like of it is permitted in the ṣila (relative clause) — or the link may be omitted, that is "from them," or the link may be generality. It may also be that the predicate is His saying: {أولئك لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ}, and His saying {إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ} a parenthetical clause. Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: "Similar to it as a parenthetical is his saying:

315-2- إنَّ الخليفةَ إنَّ اللهَ أَلْبَسَه ... سِرْبالَ مُلْكٍ به تُزْجى الخواتِيمُ
(Indeed the caliph — indeed Allah has clothed him in a robe of kingship by which seals are driven.)

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It is not necessary that «إنَّ اللهَ ألبسَه» be parenthetical, since it is possible that it be a predicate of «إنَّ الخليفة»." I say: Ibn ʿAṭiyya did not make that necessary; he only said it is like it in one of the two permissible ways. It is also possible for the two clauses — I mean His saying {إِنَّا لاَ نُضِيعُ} and His saying {أولئك لَهُمْ جَنَّاتُ} — to be two predicates of «إنَّ», according to those who allow that, meaning plurality of predicates, even if they are not in the sense of a single predicate.

Al-Thaqafī read «لا نُضَيِّع» with shadda, making it transitive by doubling as the majority made it transitive by the hamza.

semin-durr:31-31.t:
His saying: {مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ}. There are four possibilities regarding this «مِنْ». The first: that it is for beginning. The second: that it is partitive. The third: that it is for specifying the kind, that is, something of bracelets. The fourth: that it is redundant according to al-Akhfash, and His saying {وحلوا أَسَاوِرَ} [al-Insān: 21] indicates it. Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned the last three.

Asāwir is the plural of aswira, and aswira is the plural of siwār, like ḥimār and aḥmira; so it is a plural of a plural. It is a plural of iswār. He recited:

315-3- واللهِ لولا صِبْيَةٌ صِغارُ ... كأنَّما وجوهُهمْ أَقْمارُ
(By Allah, were it not for small children whose faces are as though moons,)
- أخافُ أَنْ يُصِيبهم إقتارُ ... أو لاطِمٌ ليسَ له إسْوارُ
(I fear that want would strike them, or a striker who has no bracelet,)
- لمَّا رآني مَلِكٌ جَبَّارُ ... ببابِه ما طَلَعَ النَّهارُ
(a mighty king would not have seen me at his door as the day rose.)

Abū ʿUbayda said: "It is the plural of iswār with the additional letter dropped, and its origin is asāwīr."

Abān ibn ʿĀṣim read «أَسْوِرة», the plural of siwār. These two readings, both among the mutawātir, will come in [Sūrat] al-Zukhruf, if Allah the Exalted wills, and there I shall mention the difference, if Allah wills.

Siwār is pluralised in the paucal as «أَسْوِرة» and in the plural of abundance as «سُور» with sukūn on the wāw; its origin is like quḏul and ḥumur, and it is made quiescent only because of the weak letter. It may be given ḍamma out of necessity; he said:

315-4- عن مُبْرِقاتٍ بالبُرِيْنَ وتَبْ ... دُو في الأكفِّ اللامعاتِ سُوُرْ
(...from women shining with anklets, and bracelets show on the gleaming palms.)

The lexicographers said: al-siwār is whatever is placed on the forearm of gold, silver or copper; if it is of ivory it is a qulb.

His saying: {مِن ذَهَبٍ}. It may be for specification, and may be partitive. It may be attached to an omitted [word] as an adjective of «أساوِر», so its position is genitive; and it may be attached to «يُحَلُّوْنَ» itself, so its position is accusative.

His saying: {وَيَلْبَسُونَ} is conjoined to «يُحَلَّوْن». The verb of adornment is built in the passive to announce their honour, and that others do that for them and adorn them with it, as in the saying of Imruʾ al-Qays:

315-5- غرائرُ في كِنٍّ وصَوْنٍ ونَعْمةٍ ... يُحَلِّيْنَ ياقُوتاً وشَذْراً مُفَقَّراً
(Inexperienced girls, in shelter, protection and ease, adorned with rubies and perforated gold beads.)

in contrast to wearing, since a person undertakes it himself. Adornment was put before clothing because it is more desirable to the soul.

Abān ibn ʿĀṣim read «وَيَلْبِسُونَ» with kasra on the bā'.

His saying: {مِّن سُنْدُسٍ وَإِسْتَبْرَقٍ}. «مِنْ» is for specifying the kind and is an adjective of «ثياب».

Al-sundus: the fine kind of brocade (dībāj). Al-istabraq: the thick kind of it; the two are the plurals of sundusa and istabraqa. It was said: they are not plurals. Is «istabraq» of Arabic origin, derived from barīq (gleam), or Arabised, its origin being istabra? There is disagreement among the lexicographers. It was said: al-istabraq is a name for silk. He recited, for al-Murāqqish:

315-6- تراهُنَّ يَلْبِسْنَ المشاعِرَ مَرَّةً ... وإستبرقُ الديباجُ طَوْراً لِباسُها
(You see them wearing the underclothes at one time, and at another their clothing is istabraq brocade.)

and it suits what preceded. Ibn Baḥr said: "Al-istabraq: what is woven with gold."

The pattern of «سُنْدُس» is fuʿlul and its nūn is original.

Ibn Muḥayṣin read «واسْتَبرقَ» with a hamzat al-waṣl and fatḥa on the qāf, without tanwīn. Ibn Jinnī said: "This is an oversight or like an oversight." I say: it seems he supposed that he made it diptote, and there is no basis for making it diptote, because the condition for making a foreign noun diptote is that it be a proper name, and this is a generic noun. Others have explained it as making it a past verb from barīq, with istafʿala having the sense of the bare faʿala, like qarra and istaqarra.

Al-Ahwāzī said in «al-Iqnāʿ»: "«واستبرق» with waṣl and fatḥa on the qāf wherever it occurs, he does not make it fully declinable." The apparent sense of this is that it is a noun and not a verb, and there is no basis for making it diptote, as was said earlier from Ibn Jinnī. The author of «al-Lawāmiḥ», when he mentioned the waṣl of the hamza, did not add to that but stated that it remains fully declinable, and did not mention the fatḥa of the qāf either. He said: "Ibn Muḥayṣin «واستبرق» with waṣl of the hamza in the whole Qur'an: it is possible that he dropped the hamza for lightness, contrary to analogy; and it is possible that he made it Arabic from baraqa yabruqu bariqan, its pattern being istafʿala, and when it was used as a name he treated it as a verb in the waṣl of the hamza, and as the fully inflected nouns in declension and tanwīn. Most of the exegeses hold that it is Arabic and not Arabised: it entered their speech and they arabicised it."

His saying: «مُتَّكئين» is a ḥāl. Al-arāʾik: the plural of arīka, which are couches on condition they be in canopies; if they are not, it is not called an arīka. It was said: al-arāʾik are also mattresses in canopies. Al-Rāghib said: "Al-arīka: a canopy over a couch; and it is so named either because it is made of arāk wood on the ground, or because it is a place of residence, from their saying 'he settled (araka) in the place,' and the origin of urūk is staying to graze on arāk, and then it was extended to other kinds of staying."

Ibn Muḥayṣin read «عَلَّرَائك»; that is, he transferred the vowel of the hamza to the lām of definiteness, so two like letters met — the lām of «على», whose alif was dropped because of the meeting of two quiescents, and the lām of definiteness — and he counted the vowel of transfer and assimilated one lām into the other, so the pronunciation became as you see. Similar to it is the poet's saying:

315-7- فما أصبحَتْ عَلَّرْضِ نَفْسٌ بريئةٌ ... ولا غيرُها إلا سليمانُ نالها
(No soul on the earth has become innocent, nor any other, except that Sulaymān reached it.)

He means «على الأرض». A reading close to this was mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara: «بما أُنْزِلَّيْكَ», that is, «أُنْزِلَ إليك».

[Translator's note: in the source, "الارغب" is a misprint for "الراغب" (al-Rāghib), "وراية" etc. are rendered by sense; the sequence of the three verses numbered 315-3 is printed with each hemistich-pair on a separate line and a leading dash, and is kept so here; the verse 315-4 is reproduced as printed, with its first hemistich split in the source.]

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {رَّجُلَيْنِ}. It has already been said, in [Sūrat] al-Baqara, that «ضَرَبَ» with «مَثَل» may be transitive to two objects. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: the implied form is "a parable, the parable of two men," and «جَعَلْنَا» is an explanation of «مَثَل», so it has no position; or its position may be accusative as an adjective of «رَجُلَيْن», as in your saying "I passed by two men, for one of whom a garden was made."

His saying: {وَحَفَفْنَاهُمَا}. One says: ḥaffa bi-l-shayʾ, meaning he went around it from all its sides. Al-Nābigha said:

315-8- يَحُفُّه جانِباً نِيْقٍ وتُتْبِعُهُ ... مِثلَ الزجاجة لم تُكْحَلْ مِن الرَّمَدِ
(The two sides of a mountain peak surround it, and it follows it, like a glass bottle not kohl-ed for ophthalmia.)

"The people ḥaffa around him": they became encircling his sides and his edge. "I ḥafaftuhu with it," that is, I made it encircle him.

[Translator's note: the closing quotation mark after «موضعه...» in the source is unmatched. The verse is translated tentatively, as its sense is obscure in the source.]

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {كِلْتَا}. The rule for «كلتا» has already been given in the sūra before this one. It is a mubtadaʾ, and «آتَتْ» is its predicate. It came here according to the more frequent usage, which is regard for its wording rather than its meaning.

ʿAbd Allāh [ibn Masʿūd] read — and so it is in his codex — «كلا الجَنَّتين» with the masculine, because the feminine is figurative. Then he read «آتَتْ» in the feminine, taking into account the wording «الجنتين»; this is parallel to «طَلَعَ الشمسُ وأشرقَتْ» ("the sun rose [masculine verb] and shone [feminine verb]"). Al-Farrāʾ reported another reading from him: «كلُّ الجنتين آتى أُكُلَه», returning the pronoun to its wording.

His saying: «وفجَّرْنا». The majority read it with shadda, and it is so although it is a single river, as an intensification. Yaʿqūb and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read it without shadda, which is the reading of al-Aʿmash in Sūrat al-Qamar; the shadda is clearer there because of His saying «عيوناً».

The majority read «نَهَر» with fatḥa on the hā'; Abū l-Sammāl and al-Fayyāḍ with sukūn on it.

semin-durr:34-34.t:
His saying: {وَكَانَ لَهُ ثَمَرٌ}. The discussion of it has already been given fully in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām, and it has been mentioned that «الثُّمُر» with ḍamma is wealth. Ibn ʿAbbās said: all wealth, of gold, silver, animals and other things. Al-Nābigha said:

315-9- مَهْلاً فداءً لك الأقوامُ كلُّهمُ ... وما أُثَمِّرُ مِنْ مالٍ ومِنْ وَلَدِ
(Gently! All the peoples be your ransom, and whatever I accumulate of wealth and offspring.)

It was also said: it is gold and silver specifically.

Abū Rajāʾ read «بِثَمْرِه» with fatḥa and sukūn.

His saying: «وهو يحاوِرُه» is a circumstantial clause that clarifies, since conversation does not necessarily follow from speech; for muḥāwara is the exchange of speech, from ḥāra, that is, he returned. The Exalted said: {إِنَّهُ ظَنَّ أَن لَّن يَحُورَ} [al-Inshiqāq: 14]. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

316-0- وما المرءُ إلا كالشِّهابِ وضَوئِه ... يَحُوْرُ رَماداً بعد إذ هُوَ ساطِعُ
(A man is only like the meteor and its light; it returns to ash after having been radiant.)

It may be a ḥāl from the agent or from the object.

semin-durr:35-35.t:
His saying: {جَنَّتَهُ}. It was put in the singular after mention of the dual, being content with the one because the situation is known. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "As the singular is sufficed with in place of the plural in the saying of the Hudhalī:

316-1- فالعينُ بعدَهُمُ كأنَّ حِداقَها ... سُمِلَتْ بشَوْكٍ فَهْيَ عُورٌ تَدْمَعُ
(So the eye after them — as though its pupils had been gouged with thorns — is blind, and weeps.)

One may say: that is permissible only because the broken plural runs in the manner of the feminine singular, so the pronoun in «سُمِلَتْ» and in «فهي» refers to the pupils (al-ḥidāq), not to a single pupil as he imagined."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why did He put the garden in the singular after the dual? I say: its meaning is 'he entered what was his garden,' he had no garden other than it, in the sense that he has no share in the Garden promised to the God-fearing. What he owned in this world was his garden and nothing else; and he did not intend the two gardens, nor one of them."

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "What he said cannot be conceived; for His saying «ودخل جَنَّته» is a report from Allah the Exalted that this disbeliever entered his garden, so he must have intended in the report that he entered one of his two gardens, since it is impossible that he enter both at one time." I say: whenever he claims their being entered at one time, he is bound by this impossibility from the start. As for his saying "he did not intend the two gardens nor one," it means he did not intend to specify a singular or a dual, not that he did not intend to report the entering.

Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "He put it in the singular only because both are his property and so became like a single thing."

His saying: «وهو ظالمٌ» is a ḥāl from the agent of «دَخَلَ», and «لنفسِه» is the object of «ظالمٌ», the lām being redundant in it because the governor is derivative.

«قال له صاحبُه» may be a ḥāl from the pronoun in «ظالم», that is: while he is a wrongdoer in the state of saying; and it may be resumptive, explaining the cause of the wrongdoing, and this is better.

His saying: «أَنْ تبيد», that is, perishes. He said:

316-2- فَلَئِنْ باد أهلُه ... لبِما كان يُوْهَلُ
(Even if its people have perished, it was surely inhabited.)

One says bāda yabīdu buyūdan and baydūda, like «كَيْنُونة»; the operation in it is well known, which is that one of the two yā's was dropped, and its pattern is fayʿalūla.

semin-durr:36-36.t: His saying: {خَيْراً مِّنْهَا}. Abū ʿAmr and the Kufans read «منها» in the singular, looking to the nearest thing mentioned, which is His saying «جَنَّته»; and it is in the codices of Iraq without the mīm. The rest read «منهما» in the dual, looking to the origin in His saying «جَنَّتَيْن» and «كِلْتَا الجنتين»; and it is written with the mīm in the codices of the two Sanctuaries and of Syria. Each followed the orthography of his codex.

semin-durr:37-37.t:
His saying: {مِن نُّطْفَةٍ}. Al-nuṭfa originally means a drop of clear water; one says naṭafa yanṭifu, that is, it dripped. In the ḥadīth: "He went out and his head was dripping (yanṭifu)," and in one narration, yaqṭuru, which is an explanation of it. Semen was called «nuṭfa» by analogy to that.

His saying: «رَجُلاً». There are two possibilities. One: that it is a ḥāl, and that is allowed even though it is neither transitory nor derived, because it comes after «سَوَّاك», since it was possible for Him to fashion him as other than a man. It is like their saying "Allah created the giraffe, its forelegs longer than its hind legs," and the saying of another:

316-3- فجائت به سَبْطَ العظام كأنما ... عِمامتُه بين الرِّجالِ لواءُ
(She brought him forth long-boned, as if his turban among the men were a banner.)

The second: that it is a second object of «سَوَّاك», because it carries the sense of "made you" and "turned you into," which is the apparent view of al-Ḥawfī.

semin-durr:38-38.t:
His saying: {لَّكِنَّ هُوَ الله رَبِّي}. Ibn ʿĀmir read it with the alif retained in both continuation (waṣl) and pause; the rest read it with the alif dropped in continuation and retained in pause. So the pause is agreed.

The origin of this word is «لكنْ أنا»: he transferred the vowel of the hamza of «أنا» to the nūn of «لكن» and dropped the hamza, so two like letters met and were assimilated. This is the better of the two explanations of this. It was also said: he dropped the hamza of «أنا» arbitrarily, so the two like letters met and he assimilated; but that is nothing, since the first runs in accordance with the rules. The group followed what their rules require in dropping the alif of «أنا» in continuation and retaining it in pause. It was said earlier that Nāfiʿ retains its alif in continuation before a hamza that is ḍamma, kasra or fatḥa, with a detail mentioned in al-Baqara; here he did not meet a hamza, so he is also on his principle. Had he retained the alif here, it would have been closer than another's retaining it, since he retains it in continuation in general.

As for Ibn ʿĀmir, he departed from his principle in general, since it is not his school to retain this alif in continuation in any place; he only followed the orthography. It was said earlier that this is also the dialect of Tamīm.

Its i'rab: «أنا» is a mubtadaʾ and «هو» a second mubtadaʾ, «هو» being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), and «اللهُ» a third mubtadaʾ. «ربي» is the predicate of the third; the third with its predicate is the predicate of the second, and the second with its predicate is the predicate of the first. The link between the first and its predicate is the yā' in «ربي». It is also possible that the divine Name be a badal from «هو», or an adjective, or an explicative apposition, if «هو» is made to refer back to what preceded of His saying {بالذي خَلَقَكَ مِن تُرَابٍ}, not as the pronoun of the matter, even if Abū l-Baqāʾ stated it absolutely, and it is not clear. It is also possible that «هو» be a mubtadaʾ with what follows as its predicate, and it with its predicate the predicate of «لكنَّ». It may be an emphasis of the noun, and may be a separator (faṣl). It cannot be a pronoun of the matter, because then there would be no referent in this clause that stands as predicate that goes back to the noun of «لكنَّ».

Abū ʿAmr read «لكنَّهْ» with the hā' of pause (hā' al-sakt) in pause, since the aim is to show the vowel of the nūn of «أنا»; so at one time it is shown by the alif and at another by the hā' of pause. From Ḥātim al-Ṭāʾī: "Thus my sole [state] is anah."

Ibn ʿAṭiyya said, on the authority of Abū ʿAmr: "Hārūn transmitted from him «لكنَّه هو الله» with a pronoun attached to «لكن»." I say: the apparent sense of this is that it is not a hā' of pause, but that the hā' is a pronoun, the noun of «لكن», and what is after it is the predicate. Al-Fārisī derived it in a strange way: that «لكنَّا» is «لكنَّ» and its noun, which is «نا», the origin being «لكنَّنا», one of the nūns having been dropped as in {إِنَّا نَحْنُ}; and the proper construction would have been «ربنا» and «ولا نُشرك بربِّنا». He said: "But he took the meaning into account and used the singular." This is very strange.

As for the reading of the majority, «لكنَّ» with shadda cannot be operative, because the pronoun after it occurs in the nominative form.

ʿAbd Allāh read «لكنْ أنا هو» in the original form, without transfer or assimilation. Ibn Khālawayh transmitted from him «لكنْ هو الله» without «أنا». «لكنَنَا» was also read.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "What makes it good — meaning retaining the alif in continuation — is that the alif stands as a substitute for the dropping of the hamza." [He said:] "Similar to it — meaning assimilation of the nūn of «لكن» into the nūn of «نا» after dropping the hamza — is the saying of one who said:

316-4- وتَرْمِيْنَنِيْ بالطَّرْفِ أَيْ أنت مُذْنِبٌ ... وتَقْلِيْنني لكنَّ إياكِ لا أَقْلِيْ
(You cast glances at me, as if to say 'you are at fault,' and you hate me; but you I do not hate.)

The origin is «لكنَّ أنا»; he transferred, dropped and assimilated." The Shaykh said: "What he said about the verse is not necessary, since it is possible that he dropped the noun of «لكنَّ», and its omission on the strength of a clue is frequent, as in:

316-5- فلو كنتَ ضَبِّيّاً عَرَفْتَ قَرابتي ... ولكنَّ زَنْجِيُّ عظيمُ المَشافِرِ
(Had you been a Ḍabbī you would have known my kinship, but [you are] a Zanjī with huge lips.)

that is, «ولكنَّك», and likewise here: «ولكنَني إياك»." I say: al-Zamakhsharī did not claim that this is necessary in the verse so that he could be rebutted by what he mentioned.

Close to this is what the Basrans derived in a verse which the Kufans cited against them for the permissibility of the lām of inception entering the predicate of «لكنَّ», which is:

316-6- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... ولكنَّني مِنْ حُبِّها لَعَمِيْدُ
(... but I am, from love of her, utterly overcome.)

He thus entered the lām into the predicate of «لكنَّ». The Basrans derived it on the basis that the origin is «ولكنْ إني من حبها», then he transferred the vowel of the hamza of «إني» to the nūn of «لكن» after dropping the hamza, and assimilated, as already mentioned; so the lām entered only the predicate of «إنَّ». This is on the assumption that the transmission is conceded to be sound; otherwise they said that the verse is fabricated and has no known author.

The «istidrāk» (rectification) is from His saying «أكفرْتَ»: as if he said to his brother, "You are a disbeliever" — because it is an interrogative of affirmation — "but I am a believer," like your saying "Zayd is absent but ʿAmr is present," because the absence of ʿAmr might also be supposed.

semin-durr:39-39.t:
His saying: {ولولا إِذْ دَخَلْتَ جَنَّتَكَ قُلْتَ}. «لولا» is the particle of urging (taḥḍīḍ), entering upon «قلتَ». «إذا دَخَلْتَ» is accusative by «قلتَ»; it separates between «لولا» and what it enters, and no heed is paid to that because it is not alien. You know that when the particle of urging enters upon the past it is for rebuke.

His saying: {مَا شَآءَ الله}. Two possibilities in «ما». One: that it is conditional, so it is in the position of accusative, an object necessarily placed first before «شاء», that is: whatever thing Allah wills. The response is omitted, that is: whatever Allah wills is and occurs. The second: that it is relative, meaning "that which," and in that case it has two possibilities: one, that it is a mubtadaʾ with its predicate omitted, that is: that which Allah wills exists and occurs; the second, that it is the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ, its implied form being: the matter is that which Allah willed. On every assumption, this clause is in the position of accusative by the verb "say."

His saying: {إِلاَّ بالله} is the predicate of the lā of generic negation (lā al-tabriʾa), and the clause is also accusative by the saying, that is: why did you not say these two sentences.

His saying: {إِن تَرَنِ أَنَاْ أَقَلَّ}. There are two possibilities for «أنا». One: that it is an emphasis of the yā' of the speaker. The second: that it is the pronoun of separation (ḍamīr al-faṣl) between the two objects. «أَقَلَّ» is a second object or a ḥāl according to the two views on seeing: is it of the eye or of knowledge? But if you make it of the eye, it is necessary that «أنا» be an emphasis and not a separator, because its condition is that it occur between a mubtadaʾ and a khabar, or what was originally a mubtadaʾ and a khabar.

ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar read «أَقَلُّ» in the nominative, and it is necessary that «أنا» be a mubtadaʾ and «أقلُّ» its predicate. The clause is either in the position of the second object, or in the position of ḥāl, as said earlier about seeing.

{مَالاً وَوَلَداً} is a tamyīz. The response of the condition is His saying {فعسى رَبِّي}.

semin-durr:40-40.t: His saying: {حُسْبَاناً}. Al-ḥusbān is the maṣdar of ḥasaba al-shayʾa yaḥsubuhu, that is, he counted it. Al-Zajjāj said: "That is, the punishment of reckoning (ḥusbān), that is, the account of what your hands earned." It is good. Al-Rāghib said: "It was said: its meaning is fire and punishment; but in reality it is that for which one is reckoned and then requited accordingly." This agrees with what Abū Isḥāq said, and al-Zamakhsharī leaned to it also, saying: "Al-ḥusbān is a maṣdar like al-ghufrān and al-buṭlān, meaning reckoning (ḥisāb), that is, a measure that Allah reckoned and decreed, which is the judgment of its devastation." It was also said: it is the plural of ḥusbāna, which is an arrow. In the exegesis: they are pieces of fire. And in it: they are thunderbolts.

semin-durr:41-41.t:
His saying: {أَوْ يُصْبِحَ}: it is conjoined to «يُرْسِلَ». The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "«أو يُصْبِحَ» is conjoined to His saying «ويُرْسِلَ», because the sinking of water is not caused by a heavenly affliction, unless he means by «الحُسْبان» the divine decree, in which case the morning-coming of the garden as slippery ground, or the morning-coming of its water as sunken, is caused by it."

Al-zalaq and al-ghawr are originally two maṣdars, used as descriptions for intensification.

The majority read the ghayn with fatḥa. "The water ghāra yaghūru ghawran": it receded and went into the earth. Al-Burjumī read it with ḍamma on the ghayn, a dialectal form of the maṣdar. A group read «غُؤْوراً» with ḍamma on the ghayn and the hamza and a quiescent wāw. It is also a maṣdar; one says ghāra al-māʾu ghuʾūran like jalasa julūsan.

semin-durr:42-42.t:
His saying: {يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ}. It was read «تَقَلَّبُ كَفَّاه», that is, his palms turn over. «أصبح» may be in its normal sense, and may mean «صار» (became). This is a metonymy for regret, because the regretful person does that.

His saying: {عَلَى مَآ أَنْفَقَ}. It may be attached to «يُقَلِّب», and it is made transitive by «على» only because it is made to carry the sense of "regrets."

His saying «فيها», that is, in its cultivation. It may be attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from the agent of «يُقَلَّبُ», that is: lamenting. Abū l-Baqāʾ posited it so. It is an explanation of meaning; the technical implied form is only a general "being."

His saying: «ويقولُ». It may be conjoined to «يُقَلَّبُ», and may be a ḥāl.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {وَلَمْ تَكُن لَّهُ فِئَةٌ}. The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «يَكُنْ» with the yā' (two dots below); the rest with the tā' (two dots above). Both are clear, since the feminine is figurative, and the separation makes the masculine good.

His saying: «يَنْصُرُونه». This clause may be a predicate, which is the apparent sense; and it may be circumstantial, with the predicate being the preceding prepositional phrase, and the coming of a ḥāl from an indefinite noun is justified by the preceding negation. It may be an adjective of «فئة» if we make the predicate the prepositional phrase.

He said «يَنْصُرونه» (plural) by construing according to the meaning of «فِئَة», because they are equivalent to "a people" and "the people"; had it been construed according to its wording it would be in the singular, as in the saying of the Exalted: {فِئَةٌ تُقَاتِلُ فِي سَبِيلِ الله وأخرى كَافِرَةٌ} [Āl ʿImrān: 13].

Ibn Abī ʿAbla read «تَنْصُرُه» according to the wording. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Had it been «تَنْصُره» it would have been according to the wording." I say: it has been read so, as you know.

semin-durr:44-44.t:
His saying: {هُنَالِكَ الولاية لِلَّهِ}. It is possible that the speech is complete at His saying «منتصراً» and that this is a clause cut off from what precedes. On this view, several possibilities arise in the speech. The first: that «هنالك الوَلايةُ» is assumed as a verbal clause, so «الولايةُ» is the agent of the adverbial before it, that is: sovereignty is established for Allah; and «لله» is attached to the "establishment," or to the adverbial itself because it stands in the place of the governor, or to «الولاية» itself, or to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from «الولاية». This works only on the view of al-Akhfash, in that the adverbial raises an agent without reliance.

The second: that «هنالك» is accusative as an adverbial attached to the predicate of «الولاية», which is «لله», or to what «لله» is attached to, or to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from it, the governor being the "establishment" in «لله» according to those who permit a ḥāl to precede its abstract governor; or it is attached to «الولاية» itself.

The third: that «هنالك» is made the predicate and «لله» a complement, the governor in it being what was mentioned in the first possibility.

It is also possible that «هنالك» is part of what precedes, so that the speech is not complete without it, and is governed by «منتصِراً», that is: and he was not victorious in the Hereafter, with «هنالك» pointing to it. Abū Isḥāq inclined to this. On this view the pause on «هنالِك» is complete, and the beginning is with His saying «الوَلايةُ لله», which is a clause of mubtadaʾ and khabar.

The apparent sense of «هنالك» is that it is in its basic sense of a locative adverbial, as mentioned. It was already said that the two brothers read «الوِلاية» with kasra, and the difference between it and the reading of the rest with fatḥa is in Sūrat al-Anfāl, so there is no point in repeating it.

It is related from Abū ʿAmr and al-Aṣmaʿī that the kasra of the wāw here is a mistake (laḥn). They said: because the pattern fiʿāla comes only for what is a craft or a meaning taken on as an office, and there is no taking charge of affairs here.

His saying: «الحق». Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī read «الحقُّ» in the nominative, the rest in the genitive. The nominative is in three ways: the first, that it is an adjective of «الولاية»; the second, that it is the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ, that is, it is [the truth], i.e., what We revealed to you; the third, that it is a mubtadaʾ whose predicate is implied, that is: the truth is that, which is what we said. The genitive is as an adjective of the Noble Majestic Name.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī, Abū Ḥaywa, ʿAmr ibn ʿUbayd and Yaʿqūb read «الحقَّ» in the accusative as a maṣdar confirming the content of the sentence, as in your saying: "This is ʿAbd Allāh, the truth, not the falsehood."

His saying: «عُقباً». ʿĀṣim and Ḥamza read it with sukūn on the qāf, the rest with ḍamma. It was said: two dialects, like al-quds and al-qudus. It was said: the origin is ḍamma and the sukūn is for lightness. It was said, the reverse, like al-ʿusr and al-yusr, which is contrary to what is known of the language. Its accusative, and that of «ثواباً» and «أملاً», is as tamyīz for the elative before them. Al-Zamakhsharī reported that «عُقْبى» was read with alif, which is also a maṣdar like bushrā, and it is transmitted from ʿĀṣim.

semin-durr:45-45.t:
His saying: {كَمَآءٍ}. Three possibilities are in it. The first: that it is the predicate of an implied mubtadaʾ; Ibn ʿAṭiyya posited it as "it is," that is, the life of this world. The second: that it is attached to the sense of the maṣdar, that is: a striking [of a parable] like water; al-Ḥawfī said this. Both of them build this on «ضَرَب» here being transitive to one object only. The third: that it is in the position of the second object of «اضْرِبْ», because it means «صَيَّرَ» (to make). This has already been mentioned.

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān], after reporting the two views of Ibn ʿAṭiyya and al-Ḥawfī, said: "I say: «كماء» is in the position of the second object of His saying «واضربْ», that is: make for them the parable of life, that is, its description, resembling water." I say: Abū l-Baqāʾ preceded him in this.

«أَنْزَلَناه» is an adjective of «ماء».

His saying: {فاختلط بِهِ}. Two possibilities in this bā'. One: that it is causal. The second: that it is the bā' of making transitive. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "It intertwined because of it and became dense until some of it mingled with some. It was also said: the water penetrated the plants until they were saturated and shimmered with luxuriance. The proper wording on this explanation would have been 'it mingled with the plants of the earth.' The justification for its soundness is that each of two things that mingle is described by the attribute of the other."

His saying: {فَأَصْبَحَ هَشِيماً}. «أصبح» may be in its normal sense, since most afflictions strike in the morning, as in His saying {فَأَصْبَحَ يُقَلِّبُ كَفَّيْهِ} [al-Kahf: 42], and it may mean «صار» without being restricted to the morning, as in the saying:

316-7- أَصْبَحْتُ لا أَحْمِلُ السلاحَ ولا ... اَمْلِكُ رَأْسَ البعيرِ إنْ نَفَرا
(I have become one who cannot carry a weapon, nor control the head of the camel if it bolts.)

Al-hashīm: its singular is hashīma, and it is the dry. Al-Zajjāj and Ibn Qutayba said: everything that was moist and dried. From it: {كَهَشِيمِ المحتظر} [al-Qamar: 31]. From it: "I crumbled (hashamtu) the bread"; and one says "he crumbled the tharīd," when he broke it up.

His saying: «تَذْرُوْه» is an adjective of «هَشيماً». Al-dharw: scattering; it was said, lifting.

His saying: «تَذَرُوْه» [sic] with wāw. ʿAbd Allāh read «تَذْرِيه» from al-dharī, so there are two dialects in its lām: wāw and yā'. Ibn ʿAbbās read «تُذْرِيه» with ḍamma on the tā' from idhrā'. This is possibly from al-dharw and possibly from al-dharī. The majority read «الرياح» in the plural. Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan and al-Nakhaʿī, among others, read «الرِّيحُ» in the singular.

semin-durr:46-46.t: His saying: {زِينَةُ الحياة}. «زينة» is put in the singular although it is a predicate of «بَنِين» only because it is a maṣdar; so the implied form is "possessors of adornment," since the two are made the very maṣdar for intensification, since adornment comes about through them; or in the sense of "two things that adorn." It was read anomalously «زينتا الحياة» in the dual, and its alif dropped in pronunciation because of the meeting of two quiescents, so one might imagine that «زينة الحياة» was read in the accusative.

semin-durr:47-47.t:
His saying: {وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ}. «يومَ» is accusative by an implied saying after it, its implied form being: We say to them, as We set the mountains in motion: "You have come to Us…" It was also said: by an implied "remember." It was also said: it is conjoined to «عند ربك», so it is governed by His saying «خيرٌ».

Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr and Ibn ʿĀmir read it with ḍamma on the tā' and fatḥa on the yā', in the passive; «الجبالُ» is nominative because it stands in the place of the agent, and the agent is omitted because it is known, being Allah or those of the angels He commands. This reading agrees with what is agreed upon in His saying {وَسُيِّرَتِ الجبال} [al-Naba': 20], and it is supported by ʿAbd Allāh's reading here {وَسُيِّرَتِ الجبال}, as a past passive verb.

The rest read «نُسَيِّر» with the nūn of majesty and the yā' with kasra, from sayyara with shadda; «الجبالَ» in the accusative as direct object, and this reading is in keeping with what follows it of His saying {وَحَشَرْنَاهُمْ فَلَمْ نُغَادِرْ}.

Al-Ḥasan read like the reading of Ibn Kathīr and those mentioned with him, except that it is with the yā' (two dots below) [sic] because the feminine is figurative. Ibn Muḥayṣin read — and Maḥbūb transmitted it from Abū ʿAmr — «تَسِيْر» with fatḥa on the tā' (two dots above) and quiescent yā', from sārat tasīru, and «الجبالُ» in the nominative as agent.

His saying: {وَتَرَى الأرض بَارِزَةً}. «بارزةً» is a ḥāl, since the seeing is of the eye. ʿĪsā read «وتُرى الأرضُ» in the passive, with «الأرضُ» standing in the place of the agent.

His saying: «وحَشَرْناهم». Three possibilities in it. The first: that it is a past verb meant for the future, that is: and We shall gather them; likewise {وَعُرِضُواْ} [al-Kahf: 48] and {وَوُضِعَ الكتاب} [al-Kahf: 49]. The second: that the wāw is circumstantial, and the clause is in the position of accusative, that is: We do the setting in motion while they are being gathered so that they may witness those terrors. The third: al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was «حَشَرْناهم» brought in the past after «نُسَيِّر» and «تَرَى»? I say: to indicate that their gathering is before the setting in motion and before the appearing, so that they behold those mighty terrors, as if it were said: and We had gathered them before that."

The Shaykh said: "It is preferable that the wāw be circumstantial," and he mentioned something like what I had put earlier.

His saying: «فلم نغادِر» is conjoined to «حَشَرْناهم», for it is past in meaning. Mughādara here is in the sense of ghadr, which is leaving, that is, "We did not leave." The pattern mufāʿala here carries no sharing. Treachery (ghadr) is called ghadr because by it fulfilment is left. A pool of water (ghadīr) is from that because the flood left it, that is, left it and did not come to it, or left water in it; it is pluralised as ghudur and ghudrān like raghīf and rughfān; "he made it a ghadīr" means it came to have water in it. Al-ghadīra: hair left until it grew long; the plural is ghadāʾir. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

316-8- غَدائِرُه مُسْتَشْزِراتٌ إلى العُلا ... . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . .
(Her braids are twisted upward... [the rest of the verse is omitted in the source].)

Qatāda read «فلم تُغادِرْ» with the tā' (two dots above), the agent being the pronoun of the earth, or of the leaving understood from the context. Abān read «يُغادَرْ» in the passive, «أحدٌ» in the nominative.

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «نُغْدِرْ» with ḍamma on the nūn, sukūn on the ʿayn and kasra on the dāl, from aghdara in the sense of ghadara.

[Translator's note: «بالياء من تحتُ» in the sentence on al-Ḥasan is as printed; the meaning (masculine «يُسَيَّر»/«يسيّر» rather than the feminine) is rendered by sense.]

semin-durr:48-48.t:
His saying: {صَفَّاً}. It is a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun of «عُرِضوا», and its origin is as a maṣdar. One says from it ṣaffa yaṣiffu ṣaffan, then it is applied to the group lined up.
