There is disagreement here about «صَفَّاً»: is it a singular placed where the plural is meant, since what is meant is ranks (ṣufūf)? The sound ḥadīth indicates it: "Allah will gather the first and the last on one plain, in ranks." And in another ḥadīth: "The people of Paradise are one hundred and twenty ranks; you are eighty of them." It was also said: there is an omission, that is, rank after rank. Like it is His saying in one place: {وَجَآءَ رَبُّكَ والملك صَفّاً صَفّاً} [al-Fajr: 22]. And He said in another: {يَقُومُ الروح والملائكة صَفّاً} [al-Naba': 38], meaning rank after rank, by the evidence of the other verse; so likewise here. It was also said: rather, all creatures will be a single rank, which is greater in showing power. As for the two ḥadīths, they are taken as differing conditions, since it is a long day, as He testifies in His saying {كَانَ مِقْدَارُهُ خَمْسِينَ أَلْفَ سَنَةٍ} [al-Maʿārij: 4]; so at one time they are in it a single rank and at another ranks.

His saying: {لَّقَدْ جِئْتُمُونَا}: on an implied saying, that is: and We said to them such and such. It has been mentioned that this saying is the governor of {وَيَوْمَ نُسَيِّرُ الجبال} [al-Kahf: 47]. It is also possible that this saying is implied as a ḥāl from the nominative pronoun of «عُرِضُوا», that is: they were presented, it being said to them such and such.

His saying: {كَمَا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ}, that is, a coming resembling your first creation: barefoot, naked, uncircumcised, with no wealth or children with you. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "We have raised you as We brought you into being the first time." On these two assumptions it is an adjective of the omitted maṣdar, and on the view of Sībawayh it is a ḥāl from its pronoun.

His saying: {أَلَّن نَّجْعَلَ}. «أَنْ» is the lightened one, and it is separated from its predicate because the latter is a conjugated clause that is not an invocation, by a particle of negation. «لكم» may be the second object of «جعل» in the sense of making, with «مَوْعِداً» being the first. It may also be attached to the making, or be a ḥāl from «مَوْعداً» if the making is not taken as "turning into" but as merely bringing into existence.

«بل» in His saying «بل زَعَمْتُمْ» is merely for transition, without nullification.

semin-durr:49-49.t:
His saying: {وَوُضِعَ الكتاب}. The majority read it in the passive. Zayd ibn ʿAlī read it in the active, the agent being Allah or the angel; «الكتابَ» is then accusative as a direct object. «الكتابُ» is a generic term for the books, since it is known that every person has a book particular to him. The pause at {مَالِ هذا الكتاب} has already been discussed, and how the genitive lām was written separately from its governed noun in [Sūrat] al-Nisāʾ at {فَمَا لهؤلاء القوم لاَ يَكَادُونَ} [al-Nisāʾ: 78].

«لا يغادِرُ» is a circumstantial clause from «الكتاب». The governor is the prepositional phrase because it stands in the place of the verb, or the "establishment" to which the ḥāl is attached.

His saying: «إلا أحْصاها» is in the position of accusative as an adjective of «صغيرة» and «كبيرة». The clause may be in the position of the second object, since «يُغَادِرُ» means «يترك» (leaves), and «يترك» may be transitive to two objects, as in the saying:

316-9- . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . ... فقد تَرَكْتُكَ ذا مالٍ وذا نَشبِ
(... for I have left you possessing wealth and property.)

in one of the two views.

semin-durr:50-50.t:
His saying: {وَإِذَا قُلْنَا}, that is: remember.

His saying: {كَانَ مِنَ الجن}. There are two possibilities in it. The more apparent: that it is resumptive, giving the cause, as an answer to an implied question. The second: that the clause is circumstantial, with «قد» intended with it. Abū l-Baqāʾ said this, and it is not clear.

His saying: «فَفَسَقَ». The causal sense of the fā' is apparent: the transgression was caused by his being of the jinn. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: he introduced the fā' here only because the meaning is "except Iblīs, he refused, and so transgressed." I say: if he means that His saying {كَانَ مِنَ الجن} is put in the place of His saying "he refused," it is possible though remote; and if he means that a verb was omitted to which this is conjoined, that is not correct, because it is dispensable.

His saying: «عَنْ أمر». «عن» is in its normal sense of passing beyond, and it is attached to «فَسَق», that is: he went out, passing beyond the command of his Lord. It was said: it has the sense of the bā', that is, because of His command, for He does whatever He wills.

His saying: «وذُرِّيَّتَه». The wāw may be a conjunction, which is the apparent sense, and may mean "with." «مِنْ دوني» may be attached to the taking, or to an omitted [word] as an adjective of «أَوْلِياء».

His saying: {وَهُمْ لَكُمْ عَدُوٌّ} is a circumstantial clause from the object of the taking or its agent, because it has what validates either view, namely the link.

His saying: «بِئْسَ». Its agent is an implied pronoun explained by its tamyīz. The specified object of blame is omitted, its implied form being: "an evil exchange is Iblīs and his offspring." «للظالمين» is attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from «بَدَلاً». It was also said: it is attached to the verb of blame.

semin-durr:51-51.t:
His saying: {مَّآ أَشْهَدتُّهُمْ}, that is, Iblīs and his offspring; or: I did not make the angels witness, so how do you worship them? Or: I did not make the disbelievers witness, so how do you ascribe to Me what does not befit My majesty? Or: I did not make all creation witness.

Abū Jaʿfar, Shayba and al-Sakhtiyānī, among others, read «أشهَدْناهم», in the manner of glorification.

His saying: {وَمَا كُنتُ مُتَّخِذَ المضلين}. The overt noun was placed in the position of the pronoun, since by "those who lead astray" is meant those from whom He denied making them witness the creation of the heavens; He drew attention by that to their ugly description.

The majority read «كُنْتُ» with ḍamma on the tā', as a report from Him the Exalted. Al-Ḥasan, al-Jaḥdarī and Abū Jaʿfar read it with fatḥa, as an address to our Prophet Muḥammad ﷺ. ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib, may Allah be pleased with him, read {مُتَّخِذَ المضلين}, giving the active participle tanwīn and making it govern the accusative, since the present or future is meant by it.

ʿĪsā read «عَضْداً» with fatḥa on the ʿayn and sukūn on the ḍād, a common lightening, like the saying of Tamīm: sabʿ and rajl for sabaʿ and rajul. Al-Ḥasan read «عُضْداً» with ḍamma and sukūn: he transferred the vowel of the ḍād to the ʿayn after the ʿayn lost its own vowel. From him also «عَضَداً» with two fatḥas and «عُضُداً» with two ḍammas. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk read «عِضَداً» with kasra on the ʿayn and fatḥa on the ḍād. These are dialectal forms of this word.

Al-ʿaḍud of a human being and others is well known. It is used figuratively for help and supporter, so one says "so-and-so is my ʿaḍud." From it: {سَنَشُدُّ عَضُدَكَ بِأَخِيكَ} [al-Qaṣaṣ: 35], that is, We shall strengthen your support and help.

semin-durr:52-52.t:
His saying: {وَيَوْمَ يَقُولُ}. It is governed by «اذكر» (remember), that is: and the day We say, such and such will happen. Ḥamza read «نقولُ» with the nūn of majesty, taking into account the first person in His saying «ما أَشْهَدْتُهم» to the end. The rest read it with the yā' of the third person, because of the preceding overt noble Name.

His saying: «مَوْبِقاً» is the first object of «جعل», and the second is the adverbial placed before. It is also possible that [the verb] is transitive to one, so the adverbial is attached to the making, or to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from «مَوْبَقا».

Al-mawbiq: the place of destruction. One says wabiqa yawbaqu wabaqan, that is, he perished; and wabaqa yabiqu wubūqan also: he perished; and "his sin destroyed him (awbaqahu)." From al-Farrāʾ: "Allah made their mutual bond (tawāṣul) a destruction," so he made bayn have the sense of joining, and not an adverbial, as in His saying {لَقَد تَّقَطَّعَ بَيْنَكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 94] on one view. On this basis «بينَهم» is the first object and «مَوْبِقاً» the second. Al-mawbiq here may be a maṣdar, which is the apparent sense, and may be a place.

semin-durr:53-53.t:
His saying: {مَصْرِفاً}. Al-maṣrif: the place of turning aside. The Hudhalī said:

317-0- أزهيرُ هل عَنْ شَيْبَةٍ مِنْ مَصْرِفِ ... أم لا خُلُوْدَ لباذِلٍ متكلِّفِ
(O Zuhayr, is there any turning away from grey hair, or is there no immortality for a lavish giver who strains himself?)

It may be a noun of place or of time. Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "«مَصْرِفاً»: that is, turning away (inṣirāf), and it may be a place." I say: this is an oversight, for he made the pattern maf'il with kasra on the ʿayn a maṣdar of a verb whose imperfect is yafʿil with kasra, of the sound verbs; whereas they have stated explicitly that the maṣdar of this type has fatḥa on the ʿayn, and its noun of time and place have kasra on it, as in al-maḍrab and al-maḍrib.

Zayd ibn ʿAlī, may Allah be pleased with him, read «مَصْرَفاً» with fatḥa on the rāʾ, making it a maṣdar, because the ʿayn has kasra in the imperfect, so it is like al-maḍrab in the sense of al-ḍarb. I wish Abū l-Baqāʾ had mentioned this reading and explained it as he explained before.

[Translator's note: the source writes «فتح الراء» for Zayd ibn ʿAlī's reading «مَصْرَفاً», while the Qur'anic word is printed «مَصْرِفاً» in the headings of both lines; the translation follows the description of the reading as given.]

semin-durr:54-54.t:
His saying: {مِن كُلِّ مَثَلٍ}. «مِنْ كلِّ» may be an adjective of an omitted described noun, which is the object of «صَرَّفنا», that is: We have set out a parable of every parable. «مِنْ» may be redundant, on the view of al-Akhfash and the Kufans.

His saying: «جَدَلاً» is accusative as tamyīz. His saying «أكثرَ شيءٍ», that is, the most of the things from which disputation arises, if you list them one by one; he means that the human being is more disputatious than anything that disputes, so he put «شيءٍ» in the place of "things." Is it permissible for «جَدَلاً» to be transferred from the noun of «كان», the origin being "and the disputation of man was the most of anything"? There is room for examination in this. The statement of Abū l-Baqāʾ suggests its permissibility, for he said: "There are two possibilities in it. One: that «شيئاً» here has the sense of 'disputant,' because the elative is annexed to what it is a part of, and its specification by «جَدَلاً» requires that the most be a disputant; and this is of the category of putting the general for the particular. The second: that there is an omitted element in the speech, its implied form being: and man's disputation was the most of anything; then he specified it." So his saying "its implied form being: and man's disputation was" shows that attributing «كان» to the disputation is permissible, as to the sentence; except that it needs a completion: that you speak figuratively and make the disputation have a disputation, as in their saying "a poet's poem" (shiʿrun shāʿir), meaning that man's disputation has a disputation, and it is more than the disputation of all other things.

semin-durr:55-55.t:
His saying: {وَمَا مَنَعَ}: this has already been given at the end of the sūra before it.

His saying «قُبُلاً»: the disagreement of the readers about it and the explanation of that have already been given.

semin-durr:56-56.t:
His saying: {لِيُدْحِضُواْ} is attached to «يُجَادِل». Al-idḥāḍ: causing to slip. One says "he made his foot slip (adḥaḍa)," that is, made it slip and moved it from its place. The "slipping argument" is the one with no stability because its footing shakes. Al-daḥḍ: mud, because one slips in it. He said:

317-1- أبا مُنْذِرٍ رُمْتَ الوفاءَ وهِبْتَه ... وحِدْتَ كما حادَ البعيرُ الدَّحْضِ
(Abū Mundhir, you sought to be faithful, then feared it, and swerved as the camel swerves on the slippery ground.)

Another said:

317-2- وَرَدْتُ ونَجَّى اليَشْكرِيِّ حِذارُه ... وحادَ كما حادَ البَعيرُ عن الدَّحْضِ
(I came, and the Yashkurī's caution saved him; and he swerved as the camel swerves from the slippery ground.)

"A slippery place (makānun daḥḍ)" is from this.

His saying: {وَمَا أُنْذِرُواْ}. This «ما» may be a maṣdar particle, and may mean "that which," with the returning pronoun omitted. On both assumptions it is conjoined to «آياتي».

«هُزُوا» is a second object or a ḥāl. The disagreement about «هُزُوا» has already been given. The i'rab of what follows this verse was given in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām.

semin-durr:58-58.t:
His saying: {بَل لَّهُم مَّوْعِدٌ}. «المَوْعِد» may be a maṣdar, or a time, or a place.

Al-mawʾil: the place of return, from waʾala yaʾilu, that is, he returned; and it is from taʾwīl. Al-Farrāʾ said: "Al-mawʾil: the refuge; waʾalat nafsuhu, that is, he escaped." Al-Aʿshā said:

313-7- وقد أٌخَالِسُ رَبَّ البيتِ غَفْلَتَهُ ... وقد يُحاذِرُ مِنِّي ثم ما يَئِلُ
(I may snatch the master of the house in his heedlessness, and he may be wary of me, yet he does not escape.)

that is, he does not escape. Ibn Qutayba said: "Al-mawʾil: the shelter." One says waʾala so-and-so ilā so-and-so yaʾilu waʾlan and wuʾūlan when he took shelter with him; and here it is a maṣdar.

«مِنْ دونِه» is attached to the finding, since it is transitive to one object, or to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from «مَوْئِلاً».

Abū Jaʿfar read «مَوِلا» with a wāw with kasra only. Al-Zuhrī: with a doubled wāw only. The first is more analogical, for lightness.

[Translator's note: the poetry number 313-7 is as printed in the source; it does not follow the sequence of the surrounding verses.]

semin-durr:59-59.t:
His saying: {وَتِلْكَ القرى}. The two may be a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and «أهلكناهم» is then either a second predicate or a ḥāl. It may be that «تلك» is a mubtadaʾ, with «القرى» its adjective or its explication or its badal, and «أَهْلكناها» the predicate. It may also be that «تلك» is accusative in position by an implied verb, by the construction of preoccupation (ishtighāl).

The pronoun in «أَهْلَكْناهم» refers to «أهل» that is annexed to «القرى», since the implied form is "and the people of those towns"; so he gave regard to the omitted word and returned the pronoun to it. This was already mentioned at the beginning of al-Aʿrāf.

{لَمَّا ظَلَمُواْ} may be a particle, and may be an adverbial; what is in it is known.

His saying: «لِمَهْلِكِهِمْ». ʿĀṣim read «مَهْلَك» with fatḥa on the mīm, and the rest with ḍamma; and Ḥafṣ with kasra on the lām, the rest with fatḥa. Three readings result: for ʿĀṣim two readings: fatḥa on the mīm with fatḥa on the lām, which is Abū Bakr's transmission from him; the second, fatḥa on the mīm with kasra on the lām, which is Ḥafṣ's transmission from him; and the third: ḍamma on the mīm and fatḥa on the lām, which is the reading of the rest.

As for Abū Bakr's reading, «مَهْلَك» in it is a maṣdar annexed to its agent. Abū ʿAlī allowed that it be annexed to its object, and said: "«هَلَك» is transitive without hamza," and he recited:

317-4- ومَهْمَهٍ هالكٍ مَنْ تعرَّجا
(And a wilderness fatal to whoever turns aside in it.)

so «مَنْ» is governed by «هالكٍ». People have prohibited that and said: there is no proof in the verse, since it is possible that it belongs to the category of the assimilated adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha); the origin is "hālikun man taʿarraja," so «مَنْ تعرَّج» is the agent of «هالك», then he made a pronoun of «مهمه» implied in «هالك» and put «مَنْ تعرَّج» in the accusative as «al-wajha» is put in the accusative in your saying "I passed by a man handsome in the face (ḥasani l-wajha)." Then he annexed the adjective, which is «هالك», to its object, so the annexation is from accusative, and the accusative from nominative; like your saying "Zayd is eloquent of tongue and open of hand." Were it not for the assumed accusative the annexation would be impossible, since an active participle is not annexed to its nominative. It may be said: there is no need to assume the accusative, since this runs the course of the assimilated adjective, and the assimilated adjective is annexed to its nominative; but this is built on another disagreement, which is: does the relative noun occur in the chapter of the adjective or not? The sound view is that it is allowed. The poet said:

317-5- فَعُجْتُها قِبََلَ الأخيار منزلةً ... والطيِّبي كلِّ ما التاثَتْ به الأُزُرُ
(So I turned it toward the best in standing, and the pure in all that the waist-wrappers are wrapped around.)

And the Hudhalī said:

317-6- أَسِيْلاتُ أبدانٍ دِقاقٌ خُصورُها ... وَثِيراتُ ما التفَّتْ عليها الملاحِفُ
(Smooth-bodied, slender-waisted, full in what the cloaks wrap around.)

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said of this reading of Abū Bakr: "It is a time," and did not mention anything else. Others allowed in it both time and maṣdar. It is remarkable; for whenever the ʿayn of a verb's imperfect has kasra, the maf'al takes fatḥa when the maṣdar is meant, and kasra when time and place are meant. It seems he confused it with the reading of Ḥafṣ, which has kasra on the lām as mentioned, so that the maf'il from it is for time and place.

Abū l-Baqāʾ allowed in his [Abū Bakr's] reading that the maf'il in it be a maṣdar. He said: "The kasra is anomalous in it, like al-marjiʿ." If we say it is a maṣdar, is it annexed to its agent or its object? What was said regarding the reading of his companion comes here. The derivation of Abū ʿAlī, his citing the verse, and the rebuttal of it — all this applies here.

As for the reading of the rest, it is clear. «مُهْلَك» in it may be a maṣdar annexed to its object, and may be a time; and it is remote that the object be meant by it, that is: We made for the person or group that destroyed them… 

Al-mawʿid: a maṣdar or a time.

[Translator's note: the final sentence of the translation of «وجَعَلْنا للشخصِ أو الفريقِ المُهْلِكِ منهم» is rendered as given; the source phrase is elliptical. The verse in 317-5 contains a typographical doubling («قِبََلَ») in the source.]

semin-durr:60-60.t:
His saying: {وَإِذْ قَالَ موسى}. «إذ» is accusative by «اذكر» (remember), or [it denotes] the time when he said to his young man — what We have related to you of his story occurred.

His saying: «لا أَبْرَحُ». Two possibilities in it. One: that it is the deficient verb (nāqiṣa), so it needs a predicate. The second: that it is the complete verb (tāmma), so it needs none. If it is the deficient, there are two derivations in it. One: that the predicate is omitted because it is indicated, its implied form being: "I shall not cease traveling until I reach"; except that omission of the predicate in this chapter some grammarians have stated is not permissible even with evidence, save by necessity, as in his saying:

317-7- لَهَفي عليكَ للِهْفَةٍ مِنْ خائفٍ ... يَبْغي جوارَك حينَ ليس مُجِيْرُ
(My grief for you, the grief of a frightened man seeking your protection when there is no protector.)

that is, when there is no protector in the world. The second: that there is an omitted annexed noun in the speech, its implied form being: "my journey will not cease until I reach"; then «مسير» was omitted and the yā' was put in its place, so it turned into a nominative latent [pronoun] after having been an overt one genitive in position, and «حتى أَبْلُغَ» remained as it was, being the predicate.

Al-Zamakhsharī mixed these two possibilities and made them one, but in a very fine expression, saying: "If you say: «لا أبرح», if it means «لا أَزُوْل» from baraḥa al-makān, it indicates staying, not travel; and if it means «لا أزال», a predicate is needed. I say: it means «لا أزال», and the predicate is omitted because both the situation and the speech indicate it: as for the situation, because it was a state of travel; as for the speech, because His saying «حتى أَبْلُغَ» is a set limit that calls for that of which it is the limit, so the meaning must be: [I shall not cease traveling until I reach. Another possibility, which is that the meaning is:] my journey will not cease until I reach, on the basis that «حتى أبلغَ» is the predicate; then when the annexed noun was omitted the noun annexed to was put in its place, which is the pronoun of the speaker, so the verb turned from the pronoun of the third person to the form of the speaker. This is a subtle possibility."

I say: this, for all its fineness, has an examination that is not hidden, namely: the clause that stands as predicate of «مسيري» in the original is devoid of a link that ties it to it. Do you not see that there is no pronoun in «حتى أبلغ» that refers back to «مسيري», it refers only to the latent annexed-to noun, and the like of that is not sufficient. It may be answered: the referent is omitted, its implied form being "until I reach by it," that is, by my journey.

If it is the complete verb, the meaning is: "I shall not leave what I am engaged in," in the sense of: I keep to the journey and the search, and do not part from it or abandon it, until I reach, as you say "I do not leave the place." I say: on this view also an omitted direct object is needed, as the explanation of it has preceded; so the omission is unavoidable on both assumptions, the complete and the deficient, in one of the two views of the deficient.

The majority read «مَجْمَع» with fatḥa on the mīm, which is the place of meeting; it was said, a maṣdar. Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muslim ibn Yasār read it with kasra, which is anomalous because the ʿayn of its imperfect has fatḥa.

His saying: «حُقُبا» is accusative as an adverbial, meaning a long span of time (dahr). It was said: eighty years. It was said: one year in the dialect of Quraysh. It was said: seventy. Al-Ḥasan read «حُقْباً» with sukūn on the qāf; it may be a lightening, and may be an independent dialect. It is pluralised as «أَحْقاب», like ʿunuq and aʿnāq. With the same meaning is al-ḥiqba with kasra. Imruʾ al-Qays said:

317-8- فإنْ تَنْأَ عنها حَقْبَةً لا تُلاقِها ... فإنَّك ممَّا أَحْدَثَتْ بالمُجَرِّبِ
(If you stay away from her for a span of time without meeting her, you are, as to what she has newly done, one who has experienced it.)

And al-ḥuqba with ḍamma also. The first is pluralised as ḥiqab with kasra on the ḥā', like qirab, and the second as ḥuqab with ḍamma, like qurab.

His saying: «أو أَمْضِيَ». Two possibilities in it. The more apparent: that it is conjoined to «أَبْلُغَ», meaning one of two things: either his reaching the meeting-place, or his going on for a long span. The second: that it is a limit to his saying «لا أَبْرَحُ», so it is accusative by an implied «أَنْ» after «أو» in the sense of «إلى» (until), as in "I shall surely cleave to you until you pay me my due."

The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "The meaning is: I shall not cease until I reach the meeting-place of the two seas, until I have gone on for a time in which I am certain that the meeting-place of the two seas has passed." I say: then the negated verb would be given two limits, of place and time, so both must be fulfilled together, as in "I shall surely walk to your house until noon": both limits must be realised. And the meaning the Shaykh mentioned requires that he goes on for a time in which he is certain that the meeting-place of the two seas has passed.

Abū l-Baqāʾ made «أو» here in the sense of «إلاّ» in one of the two possibilities. He said: "The second is that it means: unless I go on for a time in which I am certain that the meeting-place of the two seas has passed." What Abū l-Baqāʾ mentioned is a sound meaning; the Shaykh took this meaning and combined it with the view that it means «إلى» which requires a limit, and from there the difficulty arose.

semin-durr:61-61.t:
His saying: {نَسِيَا}. The apparent sense is the attribution of forgetting to Mūsā and his young man, meaning they forgot to check on its matter, since it was a sign for them of what they were seeking. It was said: Mūsā forgot to order him to bring it, and Yūshaʿ forgot to remind him of its matter. It was said: only Yūshaʿ forgot, and this is on an omitted annexed noun, that is, one of them forgot, as in His saying «يَخْرُجُ منهما اللؤلؤُ والمَرْجان» ("pearls and coral come out of them").

His saying: {فِي البحر سَرَباً}. «سَرَبا» is the second object of «اتَّخذ». «في البحر» may be attached to «اتَّخذ», and may be attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from the first or second object.

The hā' in «سبيلَه» refers to the fish. So does the nominative [pronoun] in «اتَّخَذَ».

semin-durr:62-62.t:
His saying: {جَاوَزَا}. Its object is omitted, that is: they passed the appointed place. It was said: they passed the meeting-place of the two seas.

His saying: «هذا» points to the journey that took place after their passing the appointed place, or the meeting-place of the two seas. «نَصَبا» is the object of «لَقِيْنا». The majority read the nūn and the ṣād with fatḥa. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUbayd ibn ʿUmayr read both with ḍamma. They are two dialects of four dialects in this word. So said Abū l-Faḍl al-Rāzī in his «Lawāmiḥ».

semin-durr:63-63.t:
His saying: {أَرَأَيْتَ}. The discussion of it was given fully in [Sūrat] al-Anʿām. Abū l-Ḥasan al-Akhfash said a fine thing about it here, which I saw fit to quote: "The Arabs removed it from its meaning entirely. They said «أَرَأَيْتَك» and «أَرَيْتَكَ» with omission of the hamza when it has the sense of 'tell me'; and when it has the sense of 'you saw', its hamza is not dropped. It is also anomalous in that you must keep the address in this sense, and you never say with it: 'Arānī Zaydan ʿAmran mā ṣanaʿa,' while you say this in the sense of 'know.' It is also anomalous in that you removed it from its place entirely, by the evidence of the entry of the fā': do you not see His saying {أَرَأَيْتَ إِذْ أَوَيْنَآ إِلَى الصخرة فَإِنِّي}? The fā' entered only after it had been removed to the sense of 'as for' or 'be alert'. The meaning is: as for when we took refuge at the rock, I forgot the fish. You also removed it to the sense of 'tell me' as we said before. And when it is in the sense of 'tell me', after it must come the noun about which information is sought, and the clause after it must have interrogation; it may also be removed to the sense of 'as for', and then after it always come the condition and adverbs of time. So His saying «فإنِّي نَسِيْتُ» means: as for when we took refuge, I… or: be alert when we took refuge; and the fā' is only a response to «أَرَأَيْتَ», because «إذْ» cannot be used for conditional requital except when joined with «ما», without disagreement."

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«أرأيتَ» means 'tell me'. If you say: what is the coherence of this speech, for each of «أرأيت», «إذ أَوَيْنا», and «فإنِّي نَسِيْتُ الحوتَ» [has no connection]? I say: when Mūsā asked for the fish, Yūshaʿ mentioned what he saw of it and what befell him of forgetting it up to that point, and he was bewildered, and began to ask Mūsā about the cause of that, as if he said: 'Do you see what befell me when we took refuge at the rock — I forgot the fish.' So he omitted that."

The Shaykh said: "Both these are missing in al-Zamakhsharī's assumption that «أرأيتَ» means 'tell me'." He means by the two what preceded in the words of al-Akhfash: that after it there must be the noun about which information is sought, and that the clause after it must have interrogation.

His saying: {وَمَآ أَنْسَانِيهُ}. Ḥafṣ read it with ḍamma on the hā'; likewise in His saying {عَلَيْهُ الله} [verse 10] in Sūrat al-Fatḥ. It was said: because the yā' here originally has fatḥa, and the hā' after a fatḥa has ḍamma, so he looked here to the origin. As for Sūrat al-Fatḥ, it is because the yā' is incidental, its origin being alif, and the hā' after an alif has ḍamma, so he looked also to the origin. The rest read with kasra, looking to the wording, for it comes after a quiescent yā'. Ḥafṣ combined in his reading the dialects of the pronoun hā': he gave the hā' ḍamma in «أنسانِيْه» without lengthening, and lengthened it with a yā' in His saying {فِيهِ مُهَاناً} [al-Furqān: 69], as will come, if Allah the Exalted wills. In the rest he read like most of the readers.

His saying: {أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ} is in the position of accusative as a badal ishtimāl from the hā' of «أنسانِيْه», that is: he made me forget mentioning it.

His saying: «عَجَباً». Several possibilities in it. The first: that it is a second object of «اتَّخذ». «في البحرِ» may be attached to the taking, or to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from the first or second object. About the agent of «اتَّخذ» there are two possibilities: one, that it is the fish, as with the first «اتَّخذ»; the second, that it is Mūsā.

The second of the two possibilities of «عَجَباً»: that it is a direct object whose governor is omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "Or he said 'a wonder!' at the end of his speech, as an expression of wonder at his state. And His saying {وَمَآ أَنْسَانِيهُ إِلاَّ الشيطان} is a parenthetical clause between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined." The apparent sense of this is that it is an object of «قال», that is, he said this word.

The third: that it is a maṣdar, so the governor is implied, its implied form being: "he marvelled at that with a marvelling."

The fourth: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, whose governor is «اتَّخذ», that is: it took its way in the sea a wondrous taking. On these three views «في البحر» is a second object of «اتَّخَذَ» if we make it transitive to two objects.

semin-durr:64-64.t:
His saying: {نَبْغِ}. Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr and al-Kisāʾī dropped the yā' of «نَبْغي» in pause, and kept it in continuation. Ibn Kathīr kept it in both states. The rest dropped it in both states, following the orthography. Its due was to be retained, and it was dropped only by analogy with the verse-endings (fawāṣil), or because omission is accompanied by omission, for «ما» is relative and its referent is omitted. This differs from the one in [Sūrat] Yūsuf, which is retained according to all; that was discussed in its place.

His saying: «قَصَصاً». Three possibilities in it. The first: that it is a maṣdar in the position of ḥāl, that is, recounting. The second: that it is a maṣdar accusative by an implied verb of its own root, that is, "they retraced a retracing." The third: that it is accusative by «ارتَدَّا», because it has the sense of "so they retraced."

Al-Kisāʾī read «أنسانِيْهِ» with imāla.

ʿAbd Allāh [read] «أَنْ أذكرَكَه». Abū Ḥaywa [read] «واتخاذَ سبيلِه», conjoining this maṣdar to the object of «اذكره».

semin-durr:65-65.t:
His saying: {عِلْماً}. It is the second object of «عَلَّمْناه». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "Had it been a maṣdar it would have been taʿlīm," meaning because its verb is of the pattern faʿʿala with shadda, and the analogical maṣdar of it is taf'īl.

{مِن لَّدُنَّا} may be attached to the verb before it, or to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from «عِلْماً».

semin-durr:66-66.t:
His saying: {على أَن تُعَلِّمَنِ}. It is in the position of ḥāl from the kāf in «أَتَّبِعُك», that is: I follow you, you bestowing your knowledge on me.

His saying: «رُشْداً» is the second object of «تُعَلِّمَني», not of His saying «ممَّا عُلِّمْتَ». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "because then there would be no referent to the relative." He means that if it is transitive to a second object other than the pronoun of the relative, it cannot be transitive to the pronoun of the relative, lest it be transitive to three; yet there must be a referent to the relative.

The disagreement of the readers about «رُشْدا» has already been given in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, and whether the two [forms] have one meaning or not.

semin-durr:68-68.t: His saying: {خُبْراً}. Two possibilities in it. One: that it is a tamyīz for His saying «تُحِطْ», transferred from the agent, since the origin is "of what your knowledge has not encompassed." The second: that it is a maṣdar for the meaning of «لم تُحِط», since it is equivalent to "he did not know it with a knowing." Al-Ḥasan read «خُبُراً» with two ḍammas.

semin-durr:69-69.t:
His saying: {وَلاَ أَعْصِي}. Four possibilities in it. The first: that it has no grammatical position because it is resumptive; there is remoteness in this. The second: that it is in the position of accusative, conjoined to «سَتَجِدُني», because it is accusative in position by the saying. The Shaykh [Abū Ḥayyān] said: "It may be conjoined to «سَتَجِدُني» and then have no grammatical position?" This is an oversight; for «ستجِدُني» is accusative in position because it is accusative by the saying, so likewise what is conjoined to it; but what misled the Shaykh was that he saw the words of al-Zamakhsharī to that effect and did not examine them, so he followed him in that; thence came the oversight. Al-Zamakhsharī said: "«ولا أَعْصِي» is in the position of accusative, conjoined to «صابراً», that is: you will find me patient and not disobedient. Or «لا» is in the position… conjoined to «سَتَجِدُني»."

The fourth: that it is in the position of accusative, conjoined to «صابراً», as its explanation has preceded.

[Translator's note: the source enumerates "first, second, fourth, fourth": a third possibility is missing and the sentence "Or «لا» is in the position… conjoined to «سَتَجِدُني»" is incomplete in the text; both are translated as they stand. The numbering of the possibilities, as printed, is the second «الثاني»…then «الرابع».]

semin-durr:70-70.t: His saying: {فَلاَ تَسْأَلْني}. The disagreement of the readers about this word has already been given in Sūrat Hūd. Abū Jaʿfar read here with fatḥa on the sīn and the lām and with shadda on the nūn, without hamza.

semin-durr:71-71.t:
His saying: {لِتُغْرِقَ}. There are two possibilities in the lām. One: that it is the lām of cause. The second: that it is the lām of result (ṣayrūra). The two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] read «ليَغْرَقَ» with fatḥa on the yā' (two dots below), sukūn on the ghayn and fatḥa on the rāʾ, with «أهلُها» in the nominative as agent. The rest read with ḍamma on the tā' (two dots above) and kasra on the rāʾ, that is: so that you drown its people, with the accusative as object. Al-Ḥasan and Abū Rajāʾ likewise, except that they gave the rāʾ shadda.

Al-safīna is well known and is pluralised as sufun and safāʾin, like ṣaḥīfa, ṣuḥuf and ṣaḥāʾif. The tā' may be dropped from it, with the plural meant, so that it is a generic noun, like thamar and balaḥ; but this made form is very rare, like jarra and jarr, and ʿimāma and ʿimām. The poet said:

317-9- متى تَأْتيه تأتي لُجَ بَحْرٍ ... تقاذَفُ في غوارِبِه السَّفينُ
(Whenever you come to it you come to a deep sea, in whose billows the ships are tossed.)

Its derivation is from al-safn, which is scraping, because it scrapes the water; as it is called "bint makhr" because it cleaves (tamkhur) the water, that is, splits it.

His saying: «إمْراً»: a great thing. One says amira al-amr, that is, it became great and grew grave. He said:

318-0- داهِيَةً دَهْياءَ إمْراً ...
(A dire calamity, a grave matter...)

semin-durr:73-73.t:
His saying: {عُسْراً}. It is a second object of «تُرْهِقْني», from arhaqahu such-and-such, when he burdened him with it and covered him with it. «ما» in «بما نَسِيْتَ» is a maṣdar particle or means "that which," with the referent omitted.

[Translator's note: the source opens with «كفعولٌ», evidently a slip for «مفعولٌ» ("an object"); rendered by sense.]

semin-durr:74-74.t:
His saying: {زاكِيَةً}. Nāfiʿ, Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read «زاكية» with alif and the yā' without shadda; the rest read without the alif and with shadda on the yā'. Whoever reads «زاكية» has the active participle in its original form; whoever reads «زَكِيَّة» has taken it to the pattern faʿīla for intensification.

Al-ghulām: one who has not reached puberty. It may be applied to the mature adult. It was said: figuratively, by regard for what he was. From it is the saying of Laylā:

318-1- شَفاها مِنَ الدَّاءِ الذي قد أصابها ... غُلامٌ إذا هَزَّ القناةَ شَفاها
(A youth cured her of the sickness that had befallen her; when he brandished the spear, he healed her.)

and another said:

318-2- تَلَقَّ ذُبابَ السَّيْفِ عني فإنني ... غلامٌ إذا هُوجِيْتُ لَسْتُ بشاعرِ
(Meet the sword's edge on my behalf, for I am a youth who, when satirised, is no poet.)

It was said: rather, it is literal, because it is from ighlām, which is outstripping, and that happens only in a human who has reached puberty. The order of the names of the human being from when he is an embryo until he becomes an old man has already been given, and praise be to Allah.

Al-Zamakhsharī said: "If you say: why was it said «حتى إذا رَكِبا في السفينةِ خَرَقَها» without a fā', and «حتى إذا لَقِيا غلاماً فَقَتَله» with a fā'? I say: He made «خَرَقَها» the response of the condition, and made «قَتَله» part of the condition, conjoined to it, and the response is «قال: أَقَتَلْتَ». If you say: why were they made to differ? I say: because the scuttling did not follow immediately upon the boarding, whereas the killing followed immediately upon meeting the boy."

His saying: {بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ}. Three possibilities in it. The first: that it is attached to «قَتَلْتَ». The second: that it is attached to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from the agent or the object, that is: you killed him wrongdoing or wronged; so Abū l-Baqāʾ posited it. It is very remote. The third: that it is an adjective of an omitted maṣdar, that is: a killing without a soul.

His saying: «نُكْراً». Nāfiʿ, Abū Bakr and Ibn Dhakwān read it with two ḍammas; the rest with a ḍamma and a sukūn. They are two dialects, or one of them is the origin. «شيئاً» may be meant as a maṣdar, that is, a coming that is abominable, and may be meant as an object, that is: you have come with an abominable matter. Is al-nukr stronger than al-imr, or the reverse? It was said: al-imr is stronger, because killing people through the scuttling is greater than killing one person. It was said: rather, al-nukr is stronger because it entails certain killing, unlike scuttling the boat, which can be remedied; therefore he said "Did I not tell you" without «لك» in the first case, with «إمراً» [sic].

[Translator's note: the last clause, «ولم يأتِ بـ لك مع إمراً», is translated as printed; the sense appears to be that «لك» is added in the second rebuke but not the first.]

semin-durr:76-76.t:
His saying: {فَلاَ تُصَاحِبْنِي}. The majority read «تصاحِبْني» from the pattern mufāʿala. ʿĪsā and Yaʿqūb read «فلا تَصْحَبَنِّي» from ṣaḥibahu yaṣḥabuhu. Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, and Ubayy, read with ḍamma on the tā' (two dots above) and kasra on the ḥā', from aṣḥaba yuṣḥibu, and its object is omitted, its implied form being: "do not make yourself my companion." Ubayy read «فلا تُصْحِبْني عِلْمَك», so the object is made explicit.

His saying: {مِن لَّدُنِّي}. The majority read with ḍamma on the dāl and shadda on the nūn. That is because they inserted the nūn of protection on «لَدُن» to protect it from kasra, preserving its sukūn, as the sukūn of the nūn of «مِنْ» and «عَنْ» was preserved, so the nūn of protection was attached to them and they say minnī and ʿannī with shadda.

Nāfiʿ [reads] with the nūn without shadda. The explanation of it: he did not attach the nūn of protection to «لَدُن». But Sībawayh prohibited that and said: "It is not permissible to bring «لَدُنْ» with the yā' of the speaker without a nūn of protection." This reading is evidence against him. If it is said: why is it not said that this nūn is the nūn of protection, and was joined to «لَدُ», a dialectal form of «لَدُن», so that the saying of Sībawayh agrees with this reading? It is said: that is not sound for two reasons. One: the nūn of protection is brought only to protect the word from kasra in order to preserve its sukūn; and without the nūn they do not make it quiescent, because the dāl has ḍamma, so there is no need for the nūn. The second: Sībawayh prohibits saying «لَدُني» with lightening. The nūn has been dropped from «عَنْ» and «مِنْ» in his saying:

318-3- أيُّها السَّائِلُ عنهم وعِنِيْ ... لستُ من قيسٍ ولا قيسٌ مِنِيْ
(O you who ask about them and about me — I am not of Qays, nor is Qays of me.)

But this reading is possible, either that the nūn in it is original, or that it is for protection, having entered upon «لَدْ» with quiescent dāl, a dialect of «لدن», so two quiescents met and the nūn of protection was given kasra in accordance with its principle. If we say the nūn is original, the sukūn is a lightening, like the sukūn of the ḍād of «عَضْد» and its like.

Abū Bakr read with sukūn on the dāl and the nūn without shadda also, but he gave the dāl an ishmām of ḍamma, drawing attention to the origin. The readers differed about this ishmām: one says it is a pointing with the organ without sound, like the ishmām that occurs in pause, and this is the known view; another says it is a pointing to the vowel perceived by the senses, so it is like rawm in meaning, meaning: bringing part of the vowel. This was already established in Yūsuf at His saying {لاَ تَأْمَنَّا} [verse 11], and in His saying in this sūra «مِن لدنه», in the reading of Shuʿba also, and a discussion has gone before whose like returns here.

ʿĪsā, and Abū ʿAmr in one transmission, read «عُذُراً» with two ḍammas. From Abū ʿAmr also «عُذْرِي» annexed to the yā' of the speaker.

{مِن لَّدُنِّي} is attached to «بَلَغْتَ», or to an omitted [word] as a ḥāl from «عُذْرا».
